questions.why: Each breakpoint is a moment where panes appear, navigation swaps and columns double [DC-L03-14].
questions.default: material for cross-platform products, tailwind for web-only; web values in rem; design compact first
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L03-14]; BOARD L03 note (Material renamed window size classes to breakpoints, May 2026).
questions.preview: the resizable frame with breakpoint ticks; the layout snaps at each one.
questions.use_avoid: decide layout by window size, never by device type or orientation [DC-L10-10; S-L10-013]; avoid breakpoints that only nudge padding.

questions.question: Should layouts stretch fluidly, switch between fixed designs, or both?

options.label: Responsive
options.effect: one fluid layout (Fluent, Material definitions) [S-L03-010, S-L03-071].

options.label: Adaptive
options.effect: distinct layouts per size (show-and-hide, levitate, reflow) [S-L03-071].

options.label: Responsive inside panes, adaptive between breakpoints; window size classes on Apple, Material breakpoints elsewhere [DC-L03-22, DC-L10-10].

questions.ask: Stretch within a layout, switch layouts at breakpoints, or both?
questions.example: Show a list-detail screen stretching, then becoming two panes at 840dp.
questions.why: Responsive layouts feel continuous; adaptive layouts feel native per device (different navigation, pane counts) [DC-L03-22, DC-L10-10].
questions.default: both, with a list-detail template that becomes two panes at expanded
questions.preview: the resizable frame; pane boundaries highlight when they change.
questions.use_avoid: use adaptive changes for pane count and navigation; avoid device-type checks that break in split view and resizable windows [S-L10-013].

questions.question: How should top-level navigation work at each size?

options.label: Bottom bar on phones (3-5), rail from 600dp, sidebar on desktop (Material; iOS floating tab bar; iPad sidebar-adaptable) [S-L08-083, S-L10-014, S-L10-025].
Sidebar at every size above compact, with groups for 7+ destinations (Carbon UI shell, Primer NavList, shadcn Sidebar) [S-L08-009, S-L08-012].
Hidden in a hamburger or drawer
options.effect: looks clean, hides scope [DC-L13-02].

questions.ask: How many top-level destinations, and should navigation be a bottom bar, rail, sidebar or top bar?
questions.example: Ask for the list of main sections; show them as a bottom bar on phone, rail on tablet, sidebar on desktop.
questions.why: The navigation container is the most recognizable part of the app's silhouette: tab bar, rail, sidebar or menu bar [DC-L14-05, DC-L08-19].
questions.default: adaptive-bar-rail-sidebar; primary navigation visible whenever width allows; at most two disclosure levels; no seven-item cap
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-19, DC-L13-02, DC-L10-09]; L13 E2 (Miller's 7 does not limit menus).
questions.preview: the person's own destination names in each container across the frame widths.
questions.use_avoid: keep destinations identical across devices and swap only the container; avoid hiding primary navigation on wide layouts [DC-L14-05; S-L13-097].

questions.question: Are your pages mostly for reading, working, or data?

options.label: Reading
options.effect: centered, max about 1280px, text measure 40-80 characters (Primer full pages 1280; Carbon editorial model) [S-L03-008, S-L03-074].

options.label: Working
options.effect: left navigation plus left-aligned content with a max width [DC-L03-16].

options.label: Data
options.effect: fluid, full width (Carbon high-density model) [S-L03-074].

options.label: Material canonical layouts; never more than three panes [S-L03-027, S-L03-026].

questions.ask: Are most pages for reading, for working in, or for scanning data?
questions.example: Show a centered article, a sidebar app page and a full-width dashboard.
questions.why: The page type decides container width and pane templates: reading pages feel like documents, working pages like tools, data pages use every pixel [DC-L03-16, DC-L03-18].
questions.control: multi-select (page types) + single choice (default pane template)
questions.default: working + list-detail; one pane below 840dp, two from 840dp, three only at 1600dp+
questions.preview: the three page types in the resizable frame.
questions.use_avoid: use fluid width for tables and dashboards; avoid full-width paragraphs [DC-L03-16, DC-L02-17].

questions.question: Which column grid and composition style?

options.label: 4 / 8 / 12 columns (compact / medium / expanded), gutter 16-24, margin 16 then 24 (Material) [S-L03-026].
4 / 8 / 16 columns, 32px gutter with wide/narrow/condensed modes (Carbon) [S-L03-002, S-L03-054].
Hierarchical or bento composition for marketing; free composition only for expressive pages [DC-L15-07].

questions.ask: Which grid, and should marketing sections use a column, modular or bento composition?
questions.example: Show a feature section as columns and as a bento grid.
questions.why: 16 columns allow asymmetric, editorial layouts; 12 give symmetric splits; bento layouts feel curated with a clear hero [DC-L03-15, DC-L15-07].
questions.default: 4 / 8 / 12 columns; column grid for app surfaces, hierarchical or bento for marketing feature sections; only layout spacing (margins, pane gaps) changes with breakpoint
questions.preview: grid overlay toggle on the frame.
questions.use_avoid: make every grid break nameable ("this hero breaks the grid to signal X"); avoid changing component spacing by breakpoint [DC-L15-07, DC-L03-17].

questions.question: Should components respond to their container or to the window?

options.label: Viewport media queries keyed to the breakpoints [S-L03-016].
Container queries (Baseline since 2025-08-14; Tailwind v4 ships 13 container sizes) [S-L03-056, S-L03-016].

questions.ask: Should components adapt to the space they sit in (container queries) or to the window width?
questions.example: Show the same card in a sidebar and in the main column.
questions.why: Container-aware components look right in any slot, such as a sidebar card vs a main-column card [DC-L03-21].
questions.default: page layout by viewport, components by container queries once multi-pane layouts exist
questions.preview: the card dragged between slots.
questions.use_avoid: use container queries for reusable components; avoid viewport queries inside components placed in panes [DC-L03-21].

questions.question: Should a signature shape from your brand appear in the UI?

options.label: Logo-derived shapes as graphic elements and icon basis (Slack, Dropbox) [S-L06-030, S-L06-024].
Mixed shapes for tension, shape morph (M3 Expressive, 35 shapes) [S-L06-009].

questions.ask: Is there a shape in your logo or brand we should echo in the UI?
questions.example: Show Slack's speech-bubble lozenge used as a graphic element.
questions.why: Curves read friendlier; sharp angles raise threat perception; a shape that breaks the pattern draws attention [DC-L06-09; S-L06-073].
questions.control: single choice (+ upload of the logo for curvature)
questions.default: one radius family derived from the logo's curvature; shape variety only in hero moments
questions.preview: the logo curvature overlaid on the button radius.
questions.use_avoid: use shape variety only in hero moments; avoid shrinking essential actions into small shapes ("smaller shapes can result in essential actions looking less important") [S-L06-009].

questions.question: How soft should corners feel?

options.label: 0-2px
options.effect: official, engineered (GOV.UK, Carbon v11 buttons) [DC-L09-01, DC-L04-02].

options.label: 4-6px
options.effect: businesslike (Fluent 4, Primer and Atlassian 6) [S-L04-007, S-L04-024, S-L04-016].

options.label: 8-12px
options.effect: friendly, modern (Polaris, Paste, Blade, Mantine v9 8px; Airbnb 12px) [DC-L09-01].

options.label: Pill
options.effect: consumer, playful, touch-first (Material 3, Spectrum 2, SLDS Cosmos; iOS 26 capsule controls) [DC-L09-01; S-L04-038].

options.label: Size-dependent (Spectrum 6-10 by size) or concentric with the container (Apple) [DC-L09-01; S-L04-035].

questions.ask: How soft should corners feel: square, slightly rounded, rounded, or pill?
questions.example: Show a button, input, card and dialog at 0, 6, 12px and pill side by side.
questions.why: Corner radius tops L09's (inferred) ranking of visual differences between systems (divergence 1), and every 2025-2026 revision got rounder [DC-L09-01; L09 A2].
questions.control: single choice + radius factor slider (0, 0.75, 1, 1.5, full)
questions.default: 6px controls, 8-12px containers
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 7 (16 of 23 control defaults at 4-8px, median 6) [L09 A1; DC-L09-01]; a radius factor slider as Radix offers [S-L09-559].
blocks: Foundations > Shape > Radius scale and default
questions.preview: the component sheet morphing as the slider moves; the focus ring follows the radius.
questions.use_avoid: use sharp corners when density and precision are brand values (data, developer tools) and pill when the brand is consumer and touch-first; avoid pill on dense, short controls, which need taller heights [DC-L04-02, DC-L09-01].

questions.question: Which radius steps should exist?

options.label: No scale; radii derived from the container through concentricity (Apple) [S-L04-035].

questions.ask: Which radius steps should the scale have?
questions.example: Show the steps with a component named under each one.
questions.why: A short scale gives a tighter, more uniform look; a long scale lets large surfaces curve more [DC-L04-01].
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L04-01]; L09 preset 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, full [L09 A1 row 7].
questions.preview: each step with the components that use it; unused steps are flagged for deletion.
questions.use_avoid: grow radius with component size; delete any step you cannot name a component for [DC-L04-01].

questions.question: Which components get which radius?

options.label: Role by component family
options.effect: xsmall 2 badges, small 4 tags, medium 6 buttons and inputs, large 8 cards, xlarge 12 modals, full for avatars [S-L04-016, S-L04-018].

options.label: None for nav and tab bars, small 2px for badges, medium, large, circular for people (Fluent 2) [S-L04-007].
Four roles
options.effect: detail 2-4, control 4-8 or full, container 8-12, overlay 12-16+, person full [DC-L04-03].

questions.ask: Should radius step up with component size, and should full circles be reserved for avatars?
questions.example: Show Atlassian's mapping: badge 2, tag 4, button 6, card 8, modal 12, avatar full.
questions.why: Scaling radius with element size keeps curvature proportional; reserving full circles for people makes circles carry meaning [DC-L04-03].
questions.default: four-roles; the radius steps up one level each time the element's height roughly doubles
questions.preview: the component sheet with each component's role labeled.
questions.use_avoid: use full radius for people and pills; avoid giving small badges and large dialogs the same radius [DC-L04-03].

questions.question: Circular corners, or Apple-style continuous corners?

options.label: Continuous curvature
options.effect: SwiftUI `.continuous`, Figma corner smoothing (iOS preset 60%) [S-L04-036, S-L04-055].

options.label: CSS `corner-shape
options.effect: squircle` as progressive enhancement (experimental, not Baseline as of 2026-08-27) [DC-L04-04].

questions.ask: Keep standard circular corners, or use continuous (squircle) corners where supported?
questions.example: Show a 24px card with a circular arc and with 60% corner smoothing, magnified.
questions.why: Continuous curves blend into edges and read softer and more "Apple" at the same nominal radius [DC-L04-04].
questions.default: circular on the web; continuous on iOS-targeted components
questions.preview: magnified corner comparison.
questions.use_avoid: use continuous corners only where brand parity with iOS matters; avoid relying on `corner-shape` for anything functional [DC-L04-04].

questions.question: How should surfaces separate from each other?

options.label: Shadow ladder
options.effect: tactile, layered (Fluent dual shadows, Polaris 7 levels, Tailwind 7) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-008, S-L04-022].

options.label: Tonal layers
options.effect: flat, calm, color-forward (Carbon layers, Material surface containers, Linear) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-058].

options.label: Borders only
options.effect: dense, technical (GOV.UK, Primer) [DC-L09-02].

options.label: 1px ring plus soft shadow (Radix, Geist, Chakra, Airbnb) [DC-L09-02].
Materials and glass
options.effect: premium, content-first (Apple Liquid Glass, Airbnb) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-032].

questions.ask: How should cards and panels separate from the page: shadows, color steps, lines, or translucent material?
questions.example: Show the same card stack with shadow, tonal, border and ring-plus-shadow treatments.
questions.why: The depth model is second on L09's (inferred) ranking of visual differences (divergence 2): shadows feel tactile, tonal feels calm, borders feel technical, glass feels premium [DC-L09-02].
questions.control: single choice (pre-filled from Q-dir-01 and Q-dir-04)
questions.default: in-page containers flat with a border or tinted fill; shadows only for things that float (menus, popovers, dialogs, drag states); in light mode a 1px ring plus soft shadow, in dark mode a lighter surface per level
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L04-10, DC-L08-15]; L09 shared pattern row 12.
questions.preview: the live stack re-rendered per option, light and dark.
questions.use_avoid: use tonal or borders for data-dense tools; avoid shadows on static in-page cards when the same color steps would do [DC-L09-02, DC-L04-10].

questions.question: How many elevation levels, and how do they look in dark mode?

options.label: 4 semantic levels (sunken, default, raised, overlay) with hover and pressed variants (Atlassian) [S-L04-017, S-L04-018].
7 levels plus special or inset (Polaris, Primer) [S-L04-022, S-L04-024].

questions.ask: How many elevation levels do you need? Four named levels is typical.
questions.example: Show sunken, default, raised and overlay surfaces in dark mode with their hex steps.
questions.why: More levels allow fine hierarchy but muddy it; most products visibly use three: resting, raised, overlay [DC-L04-11].
questions.default: 4 semantic levels backed by 4-6 shadow primitives; dark mode steps surfaces 3-5% lighter per level (Atlassian #18191A, #1F1F21, #242528, #2B2C2F)
questions.preview: the stack with each level labeled in both modes.
questions.use_avoid: components at the same level never overlap each other; avoid pure-black shadows as the only dark-mode depth cue [DC-L04-11, DC-L04-13].

questions.question: What should shadows look like?

options.label: Neutral-tinted shadow color instead of black (Polaris rgba(26,26,26), Atlassian #1E1F21) [S-L04-022, S-L04-018].

questions.ask: Soft layered shadows, a key-plus-ambient pair, or tucked-under shadows?
questions.example: Show a menu with each recipe over a white and a tinted background.
questions.why: Single hard shadows look dated; layered soft shadows look realistic; tinted shadows avoid a "dirty grey" on colored surfaces [DC-L04-12].
questions.default: 2 layers (1px contact shadow plus a soft blur scaled to elevation), neutral-tinted, alpha 8-24% in light mode; in dark mode double the alpha and add a 1px light edge ring on overlays
questions.preview: shadows on the live stack with the alpha slider.
questions.use_avoid: use one light source for every shadow; avoid single hard shadows [DC-L04-12; L15 P62].

questions.question: Should any surfaces be translucent (glass, blur)?

options.label: Opaque surfaces
options.effect: most legible and cheapest [DC-L04-15].

options.label: Glass on navigation and controls only, never on content (Apple Liquid Glass
options.effect: regular for text-heavy parts, clear over media with a 35% dim) [S-L04-032, S-L10-008].

options.label: Translucent menus and flyouts only; Mica for the window base (Fluent Acrylic) [S-L04-011, S-L04-012].
Decorative glassmorphism on cards
options.effect: flagged for legibility (NN/g) [DC-L04-15].

questions.ask: Should navigation or overlays be translucent glass, or stay solid?
questions.example: Show a toolbar over a photo: solid, regular glass, and clear glass with the 35% dimming layer.
questions.why: Translucency reads premium and OS-native in 2025-26 and keeps context visible, at the cost of lower, variable contrast [DC-L04-15, DC-L10-12].
questions.default: platform material for native chrome (glass on Apple, Mica on Windows, tonal surfaces on Android); opaque on web with optional blur plus an opaque fallback; content edge-to-edge under the bars with inset-aware components
questions.preview: the toolbar and a sheet over a busy photo with live contrast readouts; the opaque fallback shown beside it.
questions.use_avoid: use glass on the functional layer (bars, controls, sheets) only; avoid glass on reading surfaces and any translucent token without an opaque twin [S-L10-008; DC-L04-16].

questions.question: How thick are borders, and when do dividers appear?

options.label: 1 / 2 / 4px with 1 default, 2 for focus and selection (Primer, Spectrum) [S-L03-009, S-L03-044].
Inset box-shadow borders for states that change width, so layout does not jump (Primer) [S-L04-024].
Dividers
options.effect: space first, then a surface change, then 1px subtle lines (Atlassian, Apple `separator`) [S-L04-017, S-L04-032].

questions.ask: Which border widths, and should lists be separated by lines, space or surface shifts?
questions.example: Show a list separated by lines, by space and by alternating surfaces.
questions.why: 1px borders read light and precise; 2px read bolder and more accessible; more lines read more "spreadsheet" [DC-L04-07, DC-L04-08].
questions.control: editable width list + single choice (divider policy)
questions.default: 1 / 2 / 4 with inset-shadow borders for state changes; space first, lines in dense data views
questions.preview: an input switching from default to error without shifting layout.
questions.use_avoid: use lines in dense tables; avoid stacking dividers and card borders on the same edge [DC-L04-08; L15 P64].

questions.question: How dark should modal backdrops be, and how strong are state overlays?

options.label: State overlays hover 0.08, focus 0.10, pressed 0.10, dragged 0.16, disabled 0.38 (Material 3) [S-L04-003].
Stronger overlays in dark mode (Atlassian hovered 16%/pressed 32% light, 20%/36% dark) [S-L04-070].

questions.ask: How dark should the backdrop behind dialogs be, and should we use Material's standard state-overlay strengths?
questions.example: Show a dialog over the page at 30%, 45% and 60% scrim.
questions.why: Darker scrims focus attention hard; lighter scrims keep context for non-blocking sheets [DC-L04-18]. Overlay strengths set hover, press and disabled looks for every color [DC-L04-17].
questions.default: scrim 40-50% near-black in light, 50-60% in dark, tinted toward the neutral hue; Material overlay numbers, raised in dark mode
questions.preview: a dialog and a bottom sheet over the page with the slider live.
questions.use_avoid: use lighter scrims for non-blocking sheets; avoid scrims so light that the dialog's modality is unclear [DC-L04-18].

questions.question: Should motion feel quick and invisible, or physical and playful?

options.label: Productive beziers
options.effect: fast, competent, no bounce (Carbon productive `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9)`) [S-L06-002].

options.label: Productive for most interactions, expressive for 1-3 hero moments per flow (Carbon expressive; Material standard vs expressive schemes) [S-L04-075, DC-L04-19].
Springs throughout
options.effect: alive, physical, interruptible (Material spring tokens, Apple duration + bounce, Airbnb) [DC-L09-06; S-L10-024].

questions.ask: Should motion be quick and invisible, calm with a few expressive moments, or physical and bouncy?
questions.example: Open the same menu and page transition with each setting.
questions.why: Motion is L09 divergence 7: short beziers feel efficient, springs with bounce feel alive, no motion feels static but calm [DC-L09-06].
questions.default: two-mode: 7 durations 50-500ms, ease-out to enter, ease-in to exit, springs only for spatial moves in the expressive mode, bounce at or below 0.2
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 5 (all 16 systems with motion tokens stay in 100-300ms) and card heuristics [DC-L09-06, DC-L04-19]; capped at productive when Q-aud-02 is high-trust.
questions.preview: the live interactions replay on every change, with a slow-motion button.
questions.use_avoid: use expressive motion for page transitions, the primary action and alerts; avoid bounce on everyday controls and in high-trust products [DC-L06-10, DC-L04-19].

questions.question: How should springs be defined and exported?

options.label: Duration + easing only (Carbon, Fluent, Polaris, Primer) [S-L04-014, S-L04-006].
Springs split into spatial (may overshoot) and effects (critically damped, for color and opacity) (Material fast/default/slow) [S-L04-060, S-L10-024].

questions.ask: Store springs as damping and stiffness, with Apple and CSS versions derived?
questions.example: Show one spring as (dampingRatio 0.8, stiffness) and as Apple (duration, bounce) and a CSS `linear()` curve.
questions.why: Springs keep velocity when interrupted and settle naturally; DTCG has no spring type, so the storage format matters [DC-L04-22; BOARD L04/L07 note].
questions.default: (dampingRatio, stiffness) plus derived (duration, bounce) for Apple and pre-sampled `linear()` for CSS; critically damped springs for effects
questions.preview: a switch and a sheet driven by the spring, dragged and released mid-flight.
questions.use_avoid: use springs for spatial moves; avoid overshoot on color and opacity [DC-L04-22; S-L10-024].

questions.question: Which durations should exist, and should exits be faster?

options.label: 4 steps
options.effect: micro, short, medium, long (Primer) [S-L04-024].

options.label: 6 steps
options.effect: instant 0, micro 100, short 150-200, medium 250-300, long 400-500, extra 700 [DC-L04-20].

options.label: Exits 20-35% shorter than entrances (Atlassian modal 250/200; Primer 300/200) [S-L04-018, S-L04-024].

questions.ask: Keep the standard duration ladder, with exits shorter than entrances?
questions.example: Show a modal entering at 250ms and exiting at 200ms (Atlassian).
questions.why: Past about 500ms UI starts to feel slow; fast, interruptible exits respect the user's time [DC-L04-20, DC-L04-24].
questions.default: 6 steps; exits about 70-80% of the entrance; motion is interruptible and never blocks input longer than about 100ms
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L04-20, DC-L04-24]; Apple: "don't make people wait for an animation to complete" [S-L04-033].
questions.preview: a timeline of each transition with its duration; clicking mid-animation shows retargeting.
questions.use_avoid: scale duration with distance travelled; avoid standard transitions over 500ms [DC-L04-20; L13 E1].

questions.question: Which easing curves?

options.label: Standard / enter / exit (Carbon, Primer, Windows) [S-L04-014, S-L04-024, S-L04-013].
Practical vs bold (Atlassian); productive vs expressive (Carbon) [S-L04-018, S-L04-014].

questions.ask: Use role-based curves: standard, enter, exit, linear?
questions.example: Plot the four curves and animate a card with each.
questions.why: Strong decelerate curves make entrances feel fast and "arriving"; role-based sets are easiest to apply consistently [DC-L04-21].
questions.default: standard (0.2, 0, 0, 1), enter (0, 0, 0, 1) or (0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1), exit (0.3, 0, 1, 1), linear only for spinners and progress
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L04-21]; L09 shared default row 5.
questions.preview: the curve editor with a live card.
questions.use_avoid: use linear only for continuous indicators; avoid ease-in for entrances [DC-L04-21].

questions.question: Should shapes morph or use an expressive shape library?

options.label: `radius.full` token only (Atlassian, Polaris, Primer, Fluent, Carbon v12) [S-L04-006, S-L04-018].
Pill reserved for people and status (Atlassian; Carbon v12 moved tags away from pill) [S-L04-016, S-L04-031].
An expressive shape library with morphing (M3 Expressive `MaterialShapes`) [S-L04-005].

questions.ask: Keep a simple full-round token, or add expressive shapes and morphing for a few signature moments?
questions.example: Show a toggle morphing from round to square when selected (M3 Expressive).
questions.why: Pills read tappable and friendly; expressive shapes (cookies, bursts, clovers) add playfulness, best kept to avatars and hero moments [DC-L04-06].
questions.show_if: Q-shape-01 is pill or Q-motion-01 is springs
questions.default: full-token; expressive shapes only for playful brands targeting Material, limited to 1-3 signature uses
blocks: Foundations > Shape > Full round and expressive shapes
questions.preview: an avatar, a FAB and a toggle with and without morphing.
questions.use_avoid: use expressive shapes on avatars and hero moments; avoid them on dense controls [DC-L04-06].

questions.question: Which named transitions and stagger should the system ship?

options.label: Fade for in-screen enter and exit (dialogs, menus) [DC-L04-23].
Fade through for unrelated destinations such as tabs [DC-L04-23].
Shared axis x, y or z for spatial relationships (onboarding x, stepper y, parent-child z) [DC-L04-23].
A stagger token of 20-50ms, total at most 500ms [DC-L04-23].

questions.ask: Ship the four standard transitions: fade, fade-through, shared axis, container transform?
questions.example: Show a list item expanding into a detail page (container transform) and tabs switching (fade through).
questions.why: Consistent transitions make navigation legible (you can feel whether you went deeper or sideways) [DC-L04-23].
questions.default: all four plus stagger
questions.preview: each transition playable on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use OS-owned navigation transitions on native platforms; avoid custom page transitions that fight the back gesture [DC-L10-14].

questions.question: What happens when users ask for reduced motion, and how much motion does each device allow?

options.label: Replace spatial motion with opacity and color changes (MDN; WCAG's motion definition excludes color, blur and opacity) [S-L04-067, S-L04-049].
Remove all non-essential motion (WCAG 2.3.3 AAA, technique C39) [DC-L04-25].
Per device
options.effect: system transitions plus brand micro-motion on phone and desktop; subtle focus scale on TV; minimal on watch; none in cars; slow and grounded in headsets [DC-L14-08; S-L14-032].

questions.ask: When someone turns on reduced motion, should movement become gentle fades or stop entirely?
questions.example: Toggle reduced motion on the preview; a sliding panel becomes a crossfade.
questions.why: A good reduced mode still feels polished (crossfades) rather than broken (jumps); motion budgets shrink as attention narrows (none in cars) [DC-L04-25, DC-L14-08].
questions.default: replace, built as a token mode; 2.3.3 treated as a requirement although it is AAA; per-device budgets applied
questions.default_source: accessibility rule and card heuristics [DC-L04-25, DC-L14-08].
questions.preview: the reduced-motion toggle on every live interaction.
questions.use_avoid: keep feedback (color, opacity) and remove travel (translate, scale, parallax); avoid removing feedback entirely [DC-L04-25].

questions.question: Do you have UI sounds or a sonic logo?

options.label: Silent by default (most web systems; tvOS plays no alert sounds) [S-L04-074].
Sounds for rare, meaningful events, always behind mute and silent mode [S-L04-074].

questions.ask: Do you have UI sounds or a sonic logo you want in the product? Most web and productivity apps stay silent.
questions.example: Play one confirmation sound and show the mute option beside it.
questions.why: Sound is a block the builder cannot compose well; it adds confirmation but annoys in shared spaces [DC-L04-27; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: silent on web and productivity apps
questions.preview: the event list with a play button per sound and the mute state.
questions.use_avoid: use sound only for rare, meaningful events that honor silent mode; avoid sounds on web and in shared-space products [DC-L04-27].

hook.accepts: Apple notification sounds as Linear PCM, IMA4, µLaw or aLaw in .aiff, .wav or .caf under 30 seconds; Android decodes Ogg (Vorbis, Opus), WAV, MP3, AAC and FLAC [S-L17-550, S-L17-551, S-L17-552]
hook.if_no: (1) stay silent, the norm for web and productivity apps; (2) use platform system sounds (Android `SoundEffectConstants`, iOS system behavior); (3) commission a sound designer for a sonic logo, noting that repeated identical sounds feel mechanical; no verified open UI-sound library was found [S-L04-074, S-L17-553, S-L17-555].

questions.question: On native platforms, whose transitions, back behavior and haptics?

options.label: OS navigation transitions and back behavior, brand micro-motion as springs in content [DC-L10-14].
System haptics only (standard controls already play them) [S-L04-043].
A semantic haptic map of about 6 events (success, warning, error, selection, toggle, light impact) [S-L04-044, S-L04-047].

questions.ask: Use the platform's own navigation transitions and haptics, with brand motion only inside content?
questions.example: Show Android predictive back and an iOS swipe-back on the preview.
questions.why: OS-owned back gestures and transitions feel native (Android predictive back peeks behind); custom haptics feel cheap when overused [DC-L10-14, DC-L04-26].
questions.default: os-nav-brand-micro and haptics-system; a semantic map only for products with frequent confirmations
questions.preview: the event list with each haptic's platform mapping.
questions.use_avoid: use haptics sparingly ("less is more"); avoid long "buzzy" vibrations [S-L04-046; DC-L04-26].

hook.accepts: Custom haptics accept Apple AHAP (.ahap JSON, intensity and sharpness 0-1) and Android `VibrationEffect` compositions
hook.if_no: system patterns first (Apple notification, impact, selection; Android `HapticFeedbackConstants`) [S-L17-547, S-L17-548, S-L17-549].

questions.question: Which OS accessibility settings must the system honor?

options.label: VoiceOver, TalkBack and ARIA labels on every icon-only control [S-L10-075, S-L10-072].
Dynamic Type, Android font scale, browser font size [DC-L10-07].

questions.ask: Honor every OS accessibility setting: screen readers, text size, contrast, reduced transparency, reduced motion, bold text, forced colors?
questions.example: Show the preview under Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency together.
questions.why: Honoring settings changes the look for that user: thicker borders in high contrast, opaque bars under reduced transparency [DC-L10-16].
questions.default: all, with high contrast and reduced transparency as token modes
questions.preview: a settings simulator panel with each toggle applied live.
questions.use_avoid: never convey a boundary or focus state with shadow or translucency alone; avoid app-level switches that override these settings [DC-L10-16].

questions.question: Do you have a custom icon set, or should the system adopt a library?

options.label: Platform-native sets
options.effect: SF Symbols (7,000+, weight-matched to SF, 20+ scripts) and Material Symbols (variable font, 2,500+) [S-L05-006, S-L05-002].

options.label: An open-source set
options.effect: Lucide (ISC), Heroicons (MIT, 316), Phosphor (MIT, 1,248, 6 weights), Tabler (6,220), Fluent System Icons (MIT) [S-L05-029, S-L05-032, S-L05-031, S-L05-033, S-L05-014].

options.label: Your own brand set (IBM, Atlassian 1.5px at 16px, Octicons) [S-L05-017, S-L05-021, S-L05-024].
A library extended with custom domain icons drawn on its template (Material 24dp keyline template; Apple symbol template) [S-L05-001, S-L05-010].

questions.ask: Do you already have icons? If not, I'd adopt a library that matches your type and corners.
questions.example: Show the same toolbar in Lucide, Phosphor, Material Symbols and SF Symbols.
questions.why: Icons are a block the builder should not draw from scratch; native sets feel "of the platform", open sets are free and consistent, custom sets carry personality [DC-L05-01; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: platform-native on native apps, one open-source set on web; platform glyphs for system actions (share, back, close, more, search, settings), brand icons for product concepts
questions.preview: the icon sheet in context; swapping libraries updates every icon.
questions.use_avoid: use one icon family per product; avoid mixing two libraries' strokes in one toolbar [DC-L05-01, inferred].

hook.accepts: one SVG per icon on a 16 or 24px master (outlined strokes, no text), or a Figma icon library; icon fonts are accepted but converted, since fonts blur and flash (GitHub moved Octicons to SVG for this reason) [S-L05-038]
hook.if_no: (1) adopt an open-source set whose stroke and corners match the type (the default); (2) commission a designer only for domain icons the library lacks, drawn on the library's template; (3) use AI icon generators only as sketches, with the caveat that stroke, keylines and optical size rarely match across a set [inferred]. Apple's terms forbid SF Symbols or look-alikes in app icons and logos [S-L05-010].

questions.skip: yes; the default library is applied.

questions.question: Outlined or filled icons, rounded or sharp?

options.label: Outlined
options.effect: light, clean, good in dense UIs (Material, Apple toolbars, Fluent Regular) [S-L05-003, S-L05-010, S-L05-014].

options.label: Filled
options.effect: more emphasis (Apple iOS tab bars and swipe actions) [S-L05-010].

options.label: Duotone or two-tone
options.effect: decorative [DC-L05-02].

options.label: Corners matched to the radius family
options.effect: pill UIs with rounded icons, 0-2px UIs with sharp icons [DC-L05-02].

questions.ask: Outlined or filled icons, and should their corners match your rounded or sharp UI?
questions.example: Show a tab bar outlined at rest and filled when selected.
questions.why: Outline reads lighter and blends with text; filled reads bolder and is easier to spot at small sizes; icons are where the brand's shape and stroke translate into UI (Atlassian matched icon stroke to its type) [DC-L05-02, DC-L06-13].
questions.default: outlined at rest, filled plus accent color when selected (two cues that survive color blindness); corners follow Q-shape-01
questions.preview: the tab bar and toolbar with style and corner toggles.
questions.use_avoid: keep hover and pressed feedback on the container, not the glyph; avoid color-only selected states [DC-L05-06].

questions.question: How heavy should icon strokes be?

options.label: Variable weight matched to text (Material wght 100-700; SF Symbols 9 weights) [S-L05-003, S-L05-010].

questions.ask: Match icon stroke to your body text weight: about 1.5px at 16px, 2px at 24px?
questions.example: Show an icon next to a label at 1.5px and 2px strokes.
questions.why: Thin strokes look elegant but get fragile below 20px; icons should match the stem weight of the text beside them (Atlassian dropped 2px for 1.5px because 2px felt "too heavy") [DC-L05-03, DC-L06-13].
questions.default: stroke visually equal to body text weight at the paired size: about 1.5px for 14-16px text, 2px at 24px
blocks: Foundations > Iconography > Stroke and corner metrics
questions.preview: icon-label pairs at each text size with the stroke slider.
questions.use_avoid: use heavier strokes on busy or photographic backgrounds; avoid sub-1.5px strokes below 20px [DC-L05-03].

questions.question: Which icon sizes, and on which construction grid?

options.label: 24dp master, 20dp live area, 2dp padding; opsz 20-48 thins large icons (Material) [S-L05-001, S-L05-003].
16px default, 20/24/32 also, tuned to 14 and 16px text (Carbon; IBM 32px master scaled down) [S-L05-016, S-L05-017].

questions.ask: Ship 16, 20 and 24px icons on a standard 24/20/2 grid?
questions.example: Show a circle and a square icon on the keyline grid.
questions.why: Keylines make a circle icon and a square icon look the same size; pixel-hinted sizes stay crisp [DC-L05-04, DC-L05-05].
questions.default: 16, 20, 24 (plus 12 and 32 if needed), sized to the adjacent text line height; Material construction unless the master is 16 or 32
questions.preview: the icon sheet at each size, magnified to show pixel alignment.
questions.use_avoid: pixel-align at the smallest shipped size; avoid 12px icons for anything interactive [DC-L05-04, DC-L05-05].

questions.question: When do icons need labels, and what color are they?

options.label: Labels by default (Material navigation, Atlassian, Polaris) [S-L05-003, S-L05-021, S-L05-027].
Icon-only for about a dozen universal actions (search, close, more, add, delete, edit, share, settings), with a tooltip and accessible name [DC-L05-07].
Monochrome icons matching text color (Carbon 4.5:1, Fluent solid) [S-L05-016, S-L05-014].

questions.ask: Label icons in navigation, and allow icon-only buttons just for universal actions like search and close?
questions.example: Show an icon-only toolbar vs the same toolbar with labels.
questions.why: Labelled icons read calmer and clearer; icon-only toolbars read expert but ambiguous; only a handful of icons are near-universal [DC-L05-07, DC-L05-08].
questions.default: labels-default plus universal-only; one neutral icon color aliased to secondary text, semantic colors only on status icons
questions.preview: toolbar variants with a label toggle; hover shows the tooltip.
questions.use_avoid: give every icon-only control an accessible label; avoid decorative multicolor icons in UI chrome [DC-L05-07, DC-L05-08; L10 baked-in rule 9].

questions.question: Do you have an app icon?

options.label: No
options.effect: see the Hook line.

questions.ask: Do you have an app icon? If so, share the layered source; if not, I can make a clearly-marked placeholder from your logo.
questions.example: Show the icon in default, dark, clear and tinted looks on an iOS home screen and as an Android themed icon.
questions.why: The app icon is a designer-made block; on Apple it is layered and lit by Liquid Glass, on Android it is adaptive and themed [DC-L05-12; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-01 includes ios, android or desktop, or the web app is installable
questions.default: one glyph of 1-3 filled shapes on a solid or gradient background, exported as Apple layers, Android foreground/background/monochrome and PWA icons
questions.preview: a home-screen mock per platform with all appearances.
questions.use_avoid: use simple filled overlapping shapes; avoid photos, fine lines, text and baked-in shadows [DC-L05-12].

hook.accepts: layered SVG or PNG layers at 1024x1024 (watchOS 1088x1088) for Apple's Icon Composer, which applies Liquid Glass and generates default, dark, clear and tinted looks; Android adaptive foreground, background and monochrome layers; PWA maskable 512px [DC-L05-12; S-L05-042]
hook.if_no: (1) the builder generates a placeholder from the logo glyph and labels it "placeholder"; (2) commission a designer, the recommended path for a shipped app; photos, fine lines, text and baked-in effects render poorly under system lighting [DC-L05-12]. SF Symbols may not be used in app icons [S-L05-010].

questions.question: How should icons be named and shipped?

options.label: SVG source of truth generating per-framework components and native packages (Octicons, Heroicons) [S-L05-022, S-L05-038].
Icon font or variable font (Material Symbols) [S-L05-002].
Name by shape ("Shield, not security"
options.effect: Fluent; SF Symbols) [S-L05-014, S-L05-012].

options.label: Plus a function-alias layer in the component API [DC-L05-09].

questions.ask: Ship icons as SVG with per-framework components, named by shape with function aliases?
questions.example: Show `shield_24_regular.svg` aliased as `action.security`.
questions.why: SVG and native symbols render crisp at every size; icon fonts blur and flash; literal names keep one icon reusable across meanings [DC-L05-10, DC-L05-09].
questions.default: SVG source, files named `<name>_<size>_<style>`, size and color as props; name by shape with a function-alias layer; RTL behavior recorded per icon
questions.preview: the exported icon package tree.
questions.use_avoid: mirror directional icons in RTL; avoid mirroring icons that depict real objects (clocks, checkmarks) [DC-L05-09, inferred].

questions.question: How should the logo appear inside the product?

options.label: Symbol only at 24-32px in the app bar, lockup on sign-in and marketing [DC-L05-13].
Appearance brand, neutral or inverse (Atlassian Logo component) [S-L05-044].

questions.ask: Symbol-only logo in the app bar and the full lockup on sign-in?
questions.example: Show the app bar with the symbol at 24px and the sign-in page with the lockup.
questions.why: A small symbol keeps chrome quiet and product-led; a full lockup reads marketing-led; a brand-colored logo competes with primary actions [DC-L05-13].
questions.default: symbol-app-bar with neutral appearance inside dense tools; favicon set from one SVG master
questions.preview: the app bar and sign-in page.
questions.use_avoid: give a logo that acts as a link an accessible name; avoid repeating the logo throughout the UI (Apple) [DC-L05-13; S-L10-009].

questions.question: Does the product use photography, and do you have photos or a photo brief?

options.label: Documentary
options.effect: "frames from a film" (IBM lifestyle photography) [S-L05-046].

options.label: Portraiture with equal stature for every subject (IBM "democratic"; Dropbox People) [S-L05-046, S-L05-057].
Still life, product or content imagery [S-L05-046].

questions.ask: Will the product show photos? If so, do you have a library or a photo brief?
questions.example: Show a hero with a documentary-style photo and one with a studio product shot.
questions.why: Photography is a block the builder cannot make honestly; natural light and ungraded color read factual and trustworthy, graded cinematic images read emotional [DC-L05-14; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: none for tools; for consumer products, a one-paragraph photo brief (subject types, perspective, light, color treatment, casting) before commissioning or buying
questions.preview: image slots in the hero, cards and avatars with the uploaded photos, or labeled placeholders.
questions.use_avoid: use real product and people photos where trust matters; avoid stock that contradicts the brief's casting and light [DC-L05-14].

hook.accepts: JPEG, WebP or AVIF exports and a written brief; masters in RAW or TIFF are kept outside the system
hook.if_no: (1) the builder drafts the photo brief from the personality sliders for you to edit; (2) commission a photographer (best for recognizability); (3) stock against the brief: Unsplash (free commercial, no competing service) or Pexels (no implied endorsement); (4) AI images with ownership and uniqueness caveats per tool, marked as synthetic under EU AI Act Art. 50; NN/g found AI images close to stock but failing on visible artifacts and stereotypes [S-L17-529, S-L17-530, S-L17-531, S-L17-578, S-L17-126]. Neutral placeholders are used until real images arrive.

questions.question: Which aspect ratios, and can text sit on images?

options.label: One ratio per component slot (16:9 hero, 3:2 card, 1:1 avatar) [DC-L05-15].
Text beside images (IBM avoids overlays on photos) [S-L05-047].
A scrim token under text on heroes, contrast-tested against the worst-case region [S-L05-072].

questions.ask: Limit images to a few ratios like 16:9, 3:2 and 1:1, and keep text beside images rather than on them?
questions.example: Show a card grid with mixed ratios vs a fixed ratio set, and a hero with and without a scrim.
questions.why: A small ratio set gives grids a calm rhythm; text beside images reads clean and keeps photos honest, scrims read cinematic but darken them [DC-L05-15, DC-L05-16].
questions.default: 3-5 ratios, one per slot; text beside images, a scrim token only for heroes
questions.preview: the card grid and hero with live contrast readout.
questions.use_avoid: use art-directed crops per breakpoint for heroes; avoid text over busy image regions without a scrim [DC-L05-15, DC-L05-16].

questions.question: Which avatar shapes should mean what?

options.label: Circle = person, square = team or org (Primer, Fluent, Atlassian) [S-L05-066, S-L05-067, S-L05-069].
Plus a distinct shape for AI agents (Primer treats bots and agents as square) [S-L05-069].

questions.ask: Circle for people, square for teams, and a third shape for AI agents?
questions.example: Show a comment thread with a person, a team and an AI agent.
questions.why: Circles read personal, squares institutional; a distinct shape makes AI actors instantly recognizable [DC-L05-18].
questions.default: circle-square plus an agent shape if the product mixes human and AI actors; sizes 16-64 on a 4/8 rhythm with initials fallback
questions.preview: the comment thread with fallbacks (initials, placeholder) and presence dots.
questions.use_avoid: keep shape meaning consistent everywhere; avoid using the person circle for bots [DC-L05-18].

questions.question: Do you have illustrations or a mascot, and where should illustration appear?

options.label: None
options.effect: empty states use an icon and text [DC-L05-20, inferred].

options.label: Line style
options.effect: precise, calm, technical (IBM: 4px grid, at most 4 line weights, 15-degree angles) [S-L05-048, S-L05-049].

options.label: Flat
options.effect: bold and energetic (IBM) [S-L05-049].

options.label: A mascot in loading, error and empty states (Mailchimp Freddie, Duolingo Duo) [S-L06-028, S-L06-026].
Where
options.effect: spot illustrations for empty, error, celebration; low-fidelity UI for onboarding; hero and collage only on marketing (Atlassian, Dropbox) [S-L05-050, S-L05-057].

questions.ask: Do you have illustrations or a mascot? If not, should empty and error states use simple icons and text instead?
questions.example: Show an empty state with a neutral spot illustration, a mascot, and icon-plus-text.
questions.why: Illustration is a designer-made block; characters and hand-drawn styles add warmth and let the UI stay neutral, but overuse adds cognitive load [DC-L06-12, DC-L05-19, DC-L05-20].
questions.default: one style derived from the icon stroke, corner radius and palette; neutral spots for routine empty states, colorful spots only for first run and celebration; no humor in errors
questions.preview: the empty, error and success states with the uploaded art or the fallback.
questions.use_avoid: use illustration only where it has a job (IBM: "have a job to do"); avoid real screenshots in onboarding illustrations and jokes in error states [S-L05-049, S-L05-050; DC-L06-12].

hook.accepts: SVG (preferred), PNG at 2x, Lottie JSON for animated pieces, plus any illustration guidelines
hook.if_no: (1) ship honest icon-plus-text empty states; (2) commission an illustrator with a brief derived from the icon stroke and palette; (3) open sets under their exact terms: unDraw (free commercial, bans AI training and competing packs), Open Peeps and Humaaans (CC0), Blush (no resale), Storyset (credit required, no logos); (4) AI tools such as Recraft or Firefly, where ownership depends on plan, and style drifts between pieces unless one artist or a strict guide owns it [S-L17-519, S-L17-521, S-L17-522, S-L17-523, S-L17-525; inferred for drift].

questions.question: Do you need pictograms between UI icons and illustrations?

options.label: UI icons plus a pictogram library (IBM) [S-L05-049].
UI icons only; illustrations cover larger needs (Atlassian) [S-L05-050].

questions.ask: Add larger pictograms for feature grids and onboarding, drawn with the icon stroke logic?
questions.example: Show a 24px UI icon, a 64px pictogram and a 120px spot icon of the same concept.
questions.why: A pictogram tier bridges austere UI icons and full illustration, so feature grids look richer [DC-L05-11].
questions.default: a pictogram tier only with marketing surfaces, drawn with the UI icon's stroke logic scaled up
questions.preview: a feature grid with each tier.
questions.use_avoid: use pictograms on marketing and onboarding; avoid them inside dense product UI [DC-L05-11].

questions.question: Do you have animated icons, Lottie files, 3D assets or custom emoji?

options.label: Built-in symbol animation (SF Symbols Appear, Bounce, Pulse, Replace, Draw) [S-L05-010, S-L05-006].
Lottie or animated illustration for onboarding and celebration [DC-L05-21].

questions.ask: Any animated or 3D assets to include? Otherwise I'll animate icons only to confirm actions or show status.
questions.example: Show an SF Symbols bounce on a saved state and a Lottie celebration on first success.
questions.why: Animated symbols confirm actions in little space; 3D and Lottie make a product feel alive but belong to onboarding and celebration [DC-L05-21].
questions.default: symbol animation only, to confirm an action or show ongoing status; 3D and Lottie kept for onboarding, celebration and marketing
questions.preview: each asset playing in its slot, with the reduced-motion alternative.
questions.use_avoid: use animated assets for rare moments; avoid looping animation near reading content [DC-L05-21; DC-L04-25].

hook.accepts: Lottie JSON, dotLottie (v2 adds state machines and theming), After Effects via Bodymovin, Rive .riv, glTF/GLB and USDZ for 3D; PNG or SVG for emoji [S-L17-541, S-L17-542, S-L17-543, S-L17-556]
hook.if_no: motion comes from the system's motion tokens only (no signature animation); commission a motion designer for celebration moments; community Lottie assets only under their stated licenses [S-L17-544, S-L17-546].

questions.question: Where may brand graphic devices and motifs appear?

options.label: Only on expressive surfaces
options.effect: marketing, onboarding, empty states, hero moments [DC-L06-11].

questions.ask: Should brand shapes or motifs appear only on marketing, onboarding and empty states?
questions.example: Show Slack-style logo shapes on an onboarding card and absent from the product table.
questions.why: Graphic devices add recognizability and warmth; overused they clutter and compete with content [DC-L06-11].
questions.default: expressive-only
questions.preview: onboarding and a product screen with the motif on and off.
questions.use_avoid: let branding defer to content in task screens (Apple) [S-L06-008]; avoid devices behind text.

hook.accepts: SVG patterns, gradient definitions and shape SVGs, recorded as brand-expression tokens with allowed surfaces
hook.if_no: commission, or ship none; NN/g and gstack both warn that decoration standing in for content reads as generic [S-L17-004, S-L17-021].

questions.question: Which chart types and chart library?

options.label: Bar, line, area, stacked bar, donut or meter, scatter, plus a KPI big number [DC-L05-22].
Guidance grouped by question
options.effect: comparisons, trends, part-to-whole, correlations, connections, geospatial (Carbon) [S-L05-075].

options.label: Theme an existing chart library rather than building one [DC-L05-22].

questions.ask: Which charts do you need? I'd start with bar, line, area, stacked bar, donut and scatter, themed on an existing library.
questions.example: Ask for one real dashboard question ("sales by region this quarter") and show the recommended chart.
questions.why: Fewer chart types make dashboards consistent and learnable; exotic types look impressive but need more reading [DC-L05-22].
questions.default: core-6 on a themed existing library; chart chrome mapped to text and border tokens; every chart gets an insight title, direct labels, a text summary and a "view as table" option
blocks: Foundations > Data visualization > Chart types and library
questions.preview: a dashboard with the chosen types in the product's palette.
questions.use_avoid: use bars for comparison and lines for trends; avoid pie charts with more than a few slices and 3D charts [DC-L05-22, inferred].

questions.question: Do you have a voice and tone guide? If not, what 3-4 traits describe how the product talks?

options.label: Warm and relaxed, crisp and clear, ready to lend a hand (Microsoft) [S-L06-046].
Bold, optimistic, practical with a wink (Atlassian) [S-L06-060].
Custom traits on NN/g's four tone dimensions with anti-tone words [S-L06-013].

questions.ask: Do you have a voice guide? If not, give me 3-4 traits in 'X, but not Y' form and I'll draft copy examples.
questions.example: Show Mailchimp's "plainspoken, genuine" and Atlassian's "Bold, Optimistic, Practical with a wink" beside the same error message.
questions.why: Voice is constant while tone shifts by situation; the product's words and visuals must agree [DC-L06-18; S-L06-013].
questions.control: single choice + file upload or text (traits)
questions.default: drafted from the personality sliders: 3-4 traits with "but not", 3 copy examples per trait
questions.preview: the error, empty state and success message rewritten in the chosen voice.
questions.use_avoid: use the traits to decide copy disputes; avoid traits every product could claim ("simple", "friendly") without a "but not" [DC-L06-18; DC-L11-05].

hook.accepts: a PDF, Markdown file or URL of an existing style guide
hook.if_no: (1) the builder drafts traits and examples from the sliders for review; (2) have a content designer review them (22% of teams have none) [S-L11-030]; the draft is labeled as a draft until someone owns it [inferred].

questions.question: How should tone change for errors, success and first use?

options.label: By user emotion
options.effect: less bold for new or anxious users, a wink for success (Atlassian) [S-L06-060].

options.label: By situation
options.effect: straightforward for serious events, congratulatory for goals (Apple) [S-L06-052].

options.label: An NN/g four-dimension profile per content type [S-L06-013].

questions.ask: How should tone shift: serious for errors, warmer for success, gentler for new users?
questions.example: Show one error and one success message at three tone settings.
questions.why: Errors need calm visuals and plain words; success can carry illustration, motion and a wink; a joke once may amuse but a dozen times annoys [DC-L06-19; S-L06-060].
questions.default: errors serious, respectful, matter-of-fact; success as warm as the brand allows; clarity beats entertainment
questions.preview: the tone matrix with each cell's example message.
questions.use_avoid: use warmth after trust is earned (success, completion); avoid humor in errors and in high-trust categories [DC-L06-19; S-L06-060].

questions.question: Sentence case or title case?

options.label: Sentence case everywhere (Microsoft, Atlassian, Fluent) [S-L06-047, S-L06-056, S-L06-098].
Title case for headings and global nav, sentence case for buttons (Mailchimp) [S-L06-051].

questions.ask: Sentence case everywhere, or title case for headings and navigation?
questions.example: Show a nav, heading and button in "Create new project" vs "Create New Project".
questions.why: Title case reads formal and lengthens the visual texture of labels; sentence case reads casual and localizes cleanly [DC-L06-20; S-L06-052].
questions.default: sentence case everywhere; all caps only on 11-12px labels with extra tracking
questions.preview: the product screen's labels re-cased live.
questions.use_avoid: use one rule per element type everywhere; avoid all caps for sentences [DC-L06-20, DC-L02-18].

questions.question: What reading level and label length should copy target?

options.label: Command labels of 2-4 words, verb first, describing the resulting state [S-L13-036].

questions.ask: Plain language for everyone, around a 6th-8th grade level, or 10th-12th for specialist tools?
questions.example: Show one help text at grade 7 and grade 12.
questions.why: Shorter strings shrink components, truncate less and read faster; even experts prefer plain language [DC-L13-13; S-L13-091].
questions.control: single choice + number (max words per button)
questions.default: 6th-8th for consumer products, 10th-12th for expert tools; button labels 2-4 words, verb first; readability over target is a lint warning
questions.preview: a readability score beside each sample string.
questions.use_avoid: use verbs that name the result ("Save changes"); avoid branded or clever button labels [DC-L13-13, DC-L06-22].

questions.question: Which grammar and punctuation rules?

options.label: Contractions, except negative ones in high-stakes flows (GOV.UK writes "cannot") [S-L06-048].

questions.ask: Contractions yes, 'you' for the user, 'we' sparingly, and no exclamation marks in errors?
questions.example: Show "We couldn't save your file!" vs "Your file wasn't saved. Try again."
questions.why: Contractions, "we" and occasional emoji read friendlier; no negative contractions and no exclamation marks read more formal and precise [DC-L06-21].
questions.default: all four as listed
questions.preview: sample strings updating per toggle.
questions.use_avoid: keep mechanics identical across products; avoid mixing date and number formats (see Q-voice-06) [DC-L06-21].

questions.question: Which microcopy patterns and word list should components ship with?

options.label: Verb-first buttons, descriptive links (not "Click here"), blame-free fix-it errors, empty states with a next step [S-L06-052, S-L06-051].
Consistent flow vocabulary
options.effect: Get started, Continue/Next, Done [S-L06-052].

options.label: A maintained A-Z word list (Mailchimp, Microsoft) [S-L06-014, S-L06-047].
Bias-free rules
options.effect: role nouns, singular they, people's own pronouns (Microsoft; Atlassian inclusive-language page) [S-L06-102, S-L06-054].

questions.ask: Start a 20-50 term glossary and ship microcopy rules with every component?
questions.example: Ask for 5 terms users see often ("workspace" or "project"?) and show them in the nav and an empty state.
questions.why: Verb labels shorten buttons and clarify hierarchy; consistent terms make navigation and empty states predictable [DC-L06-22, DC-L06-23].
questions.default: all four; a 20-50 term glossary on day one, linted in copy; locale formats and any regulated copy recorded as fixed patterns
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L06-22, DC-L06-23]; K5.3 and K5.5 [inferred].
questions.preview: each component with its microcopy rule and an example.
questions.use_avoid: use the glossary term everywhere; avoid synonyms for the same object [DC-L06-23].

questions.question: What should your components be built on?

options.label: Headless primitives
options.effect: Radix, Base UI (v1 stable Dec 2025), React Aria, Ark UI [S-L08-030, S-L08-026, S-L08-032, S-L08-031].

options.label: Copy-in styled layer
options.effect: shadcn/ui on Base UI (its default since July 2026), Radix or React Aria [S-L08-020; BOARD L08 note].

options.label: Web components (Polaris, Fluent UI Web Components v3) [S-L08-022, S-L08-010].
Native controls themed with your tokens (SwiftUI/UIKit, Compose Material 3) [S-L08-103, S-L08-105].
Adopt a system as-is (Material, Carbon, Fluent, Untitled UI) [S-L11-078; DC-L11-01].

questions.ask: Build on headless primitives, a copy-in styled layer like shadcn, web components, native controls, or adopt a full system as-is?
questions.example: Show the same dialog built on Base UI with your tokens vs stock Material.
questions.why: Headless primitives leave every visual choice to your tokens; styled forks inherit the source's look until re-themed; native controls inherit the platform look [DC-L08-03]. Adopting a whole system makes you look like it ("websites made with shadcn/ui famously look the same") [DC-L11-01; S-L11-073].
questions.control: single choice per platform (pre-filled from Q-scope-05, Q-plat-08 and Q-tool-02)
questions.default: React web: shadcn on Base UI or React Aria; multi-framework: Ark UI or web components; mobile: native controls; small teams adapt an accessible base and invest in tokens and docs
questions.preview: the catalog re-rendered per base; a keyboard-test strip shows focus order and ARIA roles inherited.
questions.use_avoid: use accessible primitives so keyboard and ARIA behavior come for free; avoid assuming re-themed colors inherit contrast (they don't) [DC-L11-01].

questions.question: Which components are in version 1?

options.label: Core (about 25, in 8-10 of 10 benchmark systems)
options.effect: Button, Text field, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, Tabs, Tooltip, Popover, Dialog, Menu, Progress bar, Spinner, Alert/banner, Badge, Avatar, Card, List, Table, Link, Breadcrumbs, Side navigation, Accordion [DC-L08-01].

options.label: Extended (about 25 more)
options.effect: combobox, multi-select, date picker, file upload, toast, skeleton, empty state, drawer/sheet, pagination and others [DC-L08-01].

options.label: Brand and AI extras
options.effect: Logo, AI label and AI button (see Q-icon-08, Q-ai-01).

questions.ask: Start with the 25 core components most systems share, and add others when two products need them?
questions.example: Show the core 25 as a grid; ask which screens of their product need something missing.
questions.why: Completeness is the top adoption factor (79%), but a large inventory raises maintenance cost [DC-L08-01; S-L11-030].
questions.default: core-25; extended components when two or more products ask for them
questions.preview: the catalog grid with a count and a "used by" tag per component.
questions.use_avoid: use the audit (Q-scope-02) and pilot to pick extras; avoid building components no product has asked for [DC-L08-01, DC-L11-07].

questions.question: Configuration props or composable parts?

options.label: Compound parts, asChild/Slot, render props (Base UI, Radix, React Aria) [S-L08-087, S-L08-088, S-L08-089].
Figma
options.effect: variants for state, size and type; booleans for optional icons; text props for labels; instance swap for single icons; slots for repeating or freeform content [S-L07-021, S-L07-022].

questions.ask: Props for small components like Button, composable parts for containers like Dialog and Card?
questions.example: Show `<Button variant="primary">` vs `<Dialog.Root><Dialog.Title/>...</Dialog.Root>`, and a Figma card with a slot.
questions.why: Configuration keeps screens uniform; composition allows richer layouts with more variance; Figma slots let instances vary without detaching [DC-L08-04, DC-L07-22].
questions.default: configuration for leaf components, compound parts for containers; the Figma mapping as listed
questions.preview: generated code and the Figma component panel for one component.
questions.use_avoid: use slots for cards, modals and lists so instances keep receiving updates; avoid variant explosions for optional content [DC-L07-22].

questions.question: How should components be grouped and named?

options.label: Purpose categories
options.effect: action, containment, communication, navigation, selection, text input (M3) [S-L08-008].

questions.ask: Group as tokens, primitives, components, patterns and templates, with an alias table for other systems' names?
questions.example: Show "Sheet / Drawer / Side panel" mapped to one name.
questions.why: The hierarchy affects findability and consistent naming across Figma and code [DC-L08-02].
questions.default: tokens > primitives > components > patterns > templates, with an alias table
questions.preview: the catalog's sidebar regrouped per option.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical name with aliases; avoid two components for one job [DC-L08-02].

questions.question: One component set for every device, or separate sets?

options.label: One set, tokens vary by mode (Spectrum desktop/mobile values; Carbon AI presence mode) [S-L03-044, S-L14-058].
Shared foundations, separate libraries per device (Wear Compose Material 3, TV Material) [S-L10-026, S-L14-025].

questions.ask: One set with device modes for phone, tablet and desktop, plus small separate libraries for watch and TV?
questions.example: Show a phone list row next to the TV focus-row version.
questions.why: One set keeps the brand identical and cheap but risks phone-shaped components on a watch or TV [DC-L14-02].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-02 marks watch, TV or car as first-class or works
questions.default: one set for phone, tablet, desktop and web with context modes; separate small libraries for watch and TV; templates for car
questions.preview: one component across device classes.
questions.use_avoid: split a library when the input model changes (focus, crown, templates); avoid stretching phone components onto TV [DC-L14-02].

questions.question: How many button emphasis levels, and how many primary actions per view?

options.label: Primary, secondary, tertiary/outline, ghost/text, plus danger (Carbon, Fluent) [S-L08-061, S-L08-066].
5-7 levels including tonal, elevated, discovery or AI variants (M3 5; Atlassian 7 incl. Rovo) [S-L08-033, S-L08-063].

questions.ask: Four button levels plus danger, with one primary action per region?
questions.example: Show a form footer with primary, secondary, tertiary and ghost buttons, then the same with two primaries flagged.
questions.why: Three levels read calm and strict; five or six allow dense toolbars; several filled buttons flatten hierarchy and look like ads [DC-L08-05, DC-L13-18].
questions.control: single choice + toggle (one primary per region)
questions.default: four-danger; at most one high-emphasis action per region, placed after the last field in reading order; a destructive button never takes the primary role
questions.preview: the button sheet in every state, plus a form footer.
questions.use_avoid: use style, not size, to mark the preferred choice (Apple); avoid two primary buttons in one group [S-L08-039; L13 E1].

questions.question: How obvious should clickable things be?

options.label: Strong
options.effect: filled or slightly raised buttons, colored underlined links, bordered inputs, color reserved for interactive elements [S-L15-004].

options.label: Balanced
options.effect: filled primary, outline secondary, link-style tertiary, links underlined on hover [S-L15-038].

options.label: Minimal
options.effect: flat, text-only actions [DC-L15-09].

questions.ask: Strong, balanced or minimal signals that something is clickable?
questions.example: Show the same card with a filled button and underlined link vs flat text-only actions.
questions.why: Minimal signifiers look sleek but cost 22% more time and 25% more fixations to find targets (NN/g) [DC-L15-09; S-L15-004].
questions.default: balanced, with strong signifiers forced on primary actions; minimal only when density is low and layouts are conventional
questions.preview: a click-test overlay highlighting everything interactive.
questions.use_avoid: use stronger signifiers as density rises; avoid minimal signifiers in dense layouts [DC-L15-09; S-L15-004].

questions.question: What should the keyboard focus ring look like?

options.label: 2px solid ring, 2px offset, radius = component radius + offset (Atlassian `radius.focus`, Primer 2px) [S-L04-016, S-L04-024].
3px ring, 2px outer offset, -3px inner offset where outside rings would clip (Material 3) [S-L04-003].
Two-tone ring (inner white, outer dark) that is 3:1 on every surface [DC-L08-11].

questions.ask: A 2px ring with a 2px gap that follows each component's corners, in a color that shows on every surface?
questions.example: Tab through a button, input and table row with each ring style.
questions.why: Thicker, offset rings are unmistakable but louder; inner rings keep dense grids tight but can fail contrast on filled controls [DC-L04-09, DC-L08-11].
questions.default: outer-2-2 in a high-contrast brand or neutral color with light and dark values, plus a forced-colors fallback (an outline, not a box-shadow alone)
questions.default_source: card heuristics and accessibility rule [DC-L04-09, DC-L08-11; S-L10-031].
questions.preview: keyboard tab-through of the preview screen with the ring on every stop.
questions.use_avoid: show focus only for keyboard (`:focus-visible`); avoid rings that the element's own fill hides [DC-L08-11, DC-L04-09].

questions.question: Which states get their own styling, per input type?

options.label: Overlays for hover and press (Material state layers) [S-L01-005, S-L08-095].
Explicit tokens per state and variant (Carbon) [S-L08-062].
Per input context
options.effect: desktop rest/hover/focus-visible/pressed/selected/disabled; TV focused with scale and elevation; tablet pointer lift [S-L14-013, S-L14-071].

questions.ask: Style enabled, hover, focus, pressed, selected, disabled, loading and error, with each device rendering the states its inputs can trigger?
questions.example: Show a card's states on desktop vs its focused state on TV.
questions.why: Overlays give automatic states for any color; explicit tokens allow tuned brand states; TV focus is large and animated while a desktop ring is thin and static [DC-L08-09, DC-L14-06].
questions.default: style all eight states; overlays for hover and press, explicit tokens for selected and error; define states once, render the subset each context can trigger
questions.preview: the state matrix for every component.
questions.use_avoid: make hover content dismissible and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13); avoid hover-only affordances on touch [DC-L14-06].

questions.question: How should selected and active items look?

options.label: Pill-shaped indicator behind the icon (M3 navigation) [S-L08-083].
Shape morph round to square (M3 Expressive toggles) [S-L08-034].

questions.ask: Show selection with an indicator plus color, and keep brand color for actions?
questions.example: Show a tab bar with a pill indicator, an underline and a neutral fill.
questions.why: Brand-colored selection is lively; neutral selection keeps brand color meaning "action" only [DC-L08-14].
questions.default: an indicator plus color, never color alone; brand primary reserved for actions in action-dense products
questions.preview: tabs, nav rail and segmented control selected.
questions.use_avoid: use two cues for selection; avoid selection states that look like primary buttons [DC-L08-14].

questions.question: How should destructive actions look?

options.label: Solid red danger button (Carbon, Primer, shadcn destructive) [S-L08-061, S-L08-064, S-L08-065].
Danger at several emphasis levels (Carbon danger primary/tertiary/ghost) [S-L08-061].
Separate warning (significant change) and danger (final irreversible step) (Atlassian) [S-L08-063].

questions.ask: Subtle red in context, solid red only in the confirmation step?
questions.example: Show a table row's delete action and the confirmation dialog.
questions.why: Solid red draws the eye and invites mis-clicks on main screens; subtle red keeps lists calm [DC-L08-06].
questions.default: subtle danger in context, solid danger only in the confirmation step
questions.preview: a list with delete actions and the confirm step.
questions.use_avoid: use undo instead of confirmation for reversible actions (Q-form-05); avoid solid red buttons in dense lists [DC-L08-06].

questions.question: Where do icons go inside buttons?

options.label: Label left, icon right (Carbon, 16px icon) [S-L08-061, S-L08-062].
Both slots (Atlassian iconBefore/iconAfter; Primer leadingVisual/trailingVisual) [S-L08-063, S-L08-064].

questions.ask: Optional leading icons on buttons, with sentence-case verb labels?
questions.example: Show "Download" with a leading icon and Carbon-style trailing icon.
questions.why: Leading icons aid scanning; a trailing icon with a left label gives Carbon's editorial look; icon-only buttons need labels [DC-L08-08].
questions.default: optional leading icon, sentence-case verb labels
questions.preview: the button sheet with icons.
questions.use_avoid: use trailing icons for direction (next, external); avoid icon-only buttons without an accessible name [DC-L08-08].

questions.question: How should the product show that it is working?

options.label: No indicator under 1 s, looped indicator 2-10 s, percent-done over 10 s (NN/g) [S-L13-032, S-L13-031].
Skeletons for page or region loads, spinners for modules (Carbon skeletons only on containers) [S-L13-033, S-L05-071].
Spinner inside the triggering button, which keeps focus (S2 pending after 1 s; Carbon inline loading) [S-L08-067, S-L08-061].

questions.ask: Nothing under a second, skeletons for page loads, spinners for single actions, progress bars past ten seconds?
questions.example: Simulate a 0.5 s, 3 s and 12 s load on the preview.
questions.why: Skeletons make pages feel structured and faster; spinners feel generic and give no duration; response-time thresholds decide which to use [DC-L13-01, DC-L08-12].
questions.default: acknowledge within 50ms; the NN/g ladder with skeletons for first page load and in-button pending states that stay focusable
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L13-01, DC-L08-12]; BOARD L13 note (timing ladder).
questions.preview: the three simulated waits.
questions.use_avoid: use optimistic UI only when failure is rare and reversible; avoid spinners for waits under a second [DC-L13-01].

questions.question: What style should form fields have, and where do labels go?

options.label: Persistent label above, hint under the label [S-L13-066].
Placeholder as label
options.effect: rejected (memory strain, no way to check entries) [S-L13-066].

options.label: Mark whichever of required/optional is rarer, "(optional)" or "(required)" [S-L08-106].

questions.ask: Outlined or filled fields, with labels always visible above them?
questions.example: Show one field outlined, filled and underline-only, each filled in and in error.
questions.why: Filled fields feel soft and app-like, outlined feel crisp and form-heavy; placeholder-only labels cause seven known problems [DC-L08-16, DC-L13-05; S-L13-066].
questions.control: single choice (style) + single choice (label) + single choice (marking)
questions.default: outlined, top labels of 1-3 words without colons, hint under the label, the rarer of required/optional marked, `autocomplete` on personal-data fields
questions.preview: the sign-up form in each style, typed into live.
questions.use_avoid: use a visible label on every field; avoid placeholder-only labels (a lint warning) [DC-L13-05; L13 E1].

questions.question: When should forms show errors, and should the submit button ever be disabled?

options.label: On submit with an error summary that takes focus, "Error:" prefix, inline messages (GOV.UK) [S-L08-077].
On blur ("reward early, punish late")
options.effect: clear the error on the keystroke that fixes it; validate at complete length for ZIP and phone [S-L13-065, S-L13-100].

options.label: Disable submit on short forms until valid, never on long ones (Carbon) [S-L08-106].

questions.ask: Check fields when people leave them, show a summary on submit, and never disable the submit button?
questions.example: Let them type a bad email and tab away, then submit with an empty field.
questions.why: Premature errors feel hostile; on-submit keeps forms calm; disabled buttons hide why an action can't run [DC-L13-06, DC-L08-17, DC-L08-10].
questions.default: on-blur for format checks, on submit otherwise, summary plus inline for forms over about 5 fields; never-disable, with `aria-disabled` and helper text when an action truly cannot run
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L13-06, DC-L08-17, DC-L08-10]; systems disagree (see Disagreements).
questions.preview: the live form with timing toggles.
questions.use_avoid: use on-blur validation for format checks; avoid flagging a field before the person has finished typing [DC-L13-06].

questions.question: How should error messages be shown and written?

options.label: Inline field error next to the source [DC-L13-07].
Error summary at the top of the form [DC-L13-07].
Full error page for catastrophic failures [DC-L13-07].

questions.ask: Errors next to their cause, a banner only for system-level problems, a dialog only when work would be lost?
questions.example: Show a field error, a page banner and a blocking dialog for three severities.
questions.why: Inline errors keep context; banners signal system problems; dialogs interrupt; prominence should match severity [DC-L13-07; S-L13-064].
questions.default: NN/g's 13 error-message guidelines: close to the source, visible without color alone, plain words that say what happened and how to fix it
questions.preview: the three severities on the form.
questions.use_avoid: use a fix-it sentence in every error; avoid blame and jargon codes [DC-L13-07, DC-L06-22].

questions.question: Where should confirmations and notifications appear: inline, toast, banner or dialog?

options.label: Inline or banner by default; toasts only for low-stakes confirmations with undo, never auto-dismissing toasts that contain actions (Carbon matrix of 4 statuses x 7 types) [S-L08-079; DC-L13-09].
No toasts; banners and dialogs only (Primer) [S-L08-098, S-L08-012].
Toasts and flags widely (M3 snackbar, Atlassian flags) [S-L08-008, S-L08-011].

questions.ask: Inline or banner by default, toasts only for low-stakes confirmations with undo?
questions.example: Save a record and show the confirmation as inline text, a toast and a banner.
questions.why: Toasts keep layouts still but flash and vanish; banners persist and are findable; systems disagree on whether toasts belong at all [DC-L08-18, DC-L13-09].
questions.default: inline-banner; the message goes where the cause is
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-18, DC-L13-09]; systems disagree (see Disagreements).
questions.preview: the save action with each channel.
questions.use_avoid: use toasts only for reversible, low-stakes results; avoid a toast as the only record of an error [DC-L13-09].

questions.question: For destructive actions, undo or confirm?

options.label: Undo with soft delete or trash for reversible actions (NN/g calls undo superior; Shneiderman rule 6) [S-L13-067, S-L13-037].
Confirmation dialog with specific verb labels, Cancel as the safe default [S-L13-067; DC-L13-08].
Undo for reversible, confirm for irreversible and costly [DC-L13-08].

questions.ask: Offer undo for anything reversible, and confirm only irreversible or costly actions?
questions.example: Delete a list item: show the undo toast, then an irreversible delete with a "Delete file / Keep file" dialog.
questions.why: Undo keeps flow fast and calm; frequent confirmations feel bureaucratic and stop being read [DC-L13-08; S-L13-067].
questions.default: both
questions.preview: the list delete flow per option.
questions.use_avoid: use verb labels on confirmations; avoid "Are you sure?" dialogs for reversible actions [DC-L13-08].

questions.question: When should the product use a dialog, a sheet or a popover?

options.label: Modal only with a clear benefit; sheets and popovers for scoped tasks; full-screen for immersive multi-step tasks (HIG) [S-L08-086].
Bottom and side sheets, drawers and panels (M3, Fluent, Atlassian) [S-L08-008, S-L08-010, S-L08-011].

questions.ask: Dialogs for short decisions, side sheets for editing with context, bottom sheets on phones?
questions.example: Edit a record in a dialog vs a side sheet on the preview.
questions.why: Centered dialogs interrupt strongly; side sheets keep context visible; popovers feel lightweight [DC-L08-20].
questions.default: dialog for short decisions, side sheet for editing with context, bottom sheet on phones; each platform's button order
