questions.preview: the same edit task in each overlay.
questions.use_avoid: use a dismiss path on every dialog (missing one is a lint error); avoid stacking modals [DC-L08-20; L13 E1].

questions.question: How should long lists load: pages, "load more", or infinite scroll?
questions.ask: Pagination for tables, load more for results, infinite scroll only for feeds?
questions.example: Show a table with pagination and a feed with infinite scroll.
questions.why: Pagination gives landmarks; infinite scroll feels endless; "Load more" keeps the footer reachable [DC-L08-21].
questions.default: pagination for tables and goal-directed search, load more for result lists, infinite scroll only for feeds
questions.preview: each collection type on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use pagination where people need to return to a position; avoid infinite scroll above a footer people need [DC-L08-21].

questions.question: How much should be visible up front, and how much behind "more"?

options.label: Progressive disclosure, at most two levels, trigger label says what is behind it [S-L13-063].
Staged disclosure (wizard or stepper), for independent steps only [S-L13-063].
Contextual reveal on hover or selection [DC-L13-03].

questions.ask: Show primary options up front and advanced ones behind a clearly labeled trigger, at most two levels deep?
questions.example: Show a settings page with an "Advanced" section collapsed and expanded.
questions.why: Progressive disclosure gives calmer, shorter screens; everything-visible reads powerful but dense [DC-L13-03].
questions.default: progressive
questions.preview: the settings page per option.
questions.use_avoid: use steppers that show position and total; avoid more than two disclosure levels (a lint warning) [DC-L13-03; L13 E1].

questions.question: How should empty states and first-time use work?

options.label: Empty states for first use, user-cleared, no results, no permission or error (Primer Blankslate, Spectrum IllustratedMessage, shadcn Empty) [DC-L13-10; S-L08-012, S-L08-015, S-L08-018].
No onboarding
options.effect: a self-evident UI (NN/g's first recommendation) [S-L13-070].

options.label: Contextual help and empty-state guidance at the moment of need [S-L13-070].
Interactive walkthrough, only for genuinely new, complex interfaces [S-L13-070].

questions.ask: Designed empty states with a next step, and contextual tips instead of a forced tour?
questions.example: Show a first-use empty project list, a no-results search and a tour with a skip button.
questions.why: A designed empty state teaches and invites; a blank area looks broken; forced tours add friction up front [DC-L13-10, DC-L13-11].
questions.default: every collection gets empty variants that state status, help learning and give a direct action; contextual onboarding; everything skippable
questions.preview: each empty-state kind with the illustration choice from Q-img-04.
questions.use_avoid: use an empty state on every collection (missing one is a lint warning); avoid tours without a skip control [DC-L13-10, DC-L13-11; L13 E1].

questions.question: Which deceptive patterns should the builder block?

options.label: Documented policy against the 16 types at deceptive.design (sneaking, forced action, hard to cancel, preselection, fake urgency, confirmshaming ...) [S-L13-071].
Documented and enforced where detectable
options.effect: pre-checked consent or marketing boxes and unequal accept/reject emphasis are lint errors; re-prompting after dismissal is flagged [S-L13-071, S-L13-108].

questions.ask: Block the deceptive patterns a machine can detect, like pre-checked marketing boxes and consent buttons with unequal emphasis?
questions.example: Show a consent dialog with equal buttons vs a "confirmshaming" one, flagged.
questions.why: Ethical defaults give accept and decline equal visual weight, leave opt-ins unchecked and keep decline copy neutral [DC-L13-15].
questions.default: enforced
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L13-15]; L13 E1 lint errors.
questions.preview: a consent dialog and a cancellation flow checked live.
questions.use_avoid: use equal emphasis for accept and reject; avoid nagging and fake urgency (the Zeigarnik effect does not justify nags) [DC-L13-15; L13 E2].

questions.question: What should appear on glanceable surfaces (widgets, tiles, complications)?

options.label: Complication = one datum, notification = urgent event, tile = one or two items, app = everything (Google) [S-L14-015].
Complications, Smart Stack, Live Activities, CarPlay widgets [S-L14-001, S-L14-047].

questions.ask: What single number or status should people see without opening the app?
questions.example: Ask for the one metric; show it as a watch complication and a home-screen widget.
questions.why: Glance surfaces look like data, not UI: big numerals, one metric, a status color, almost no chrome [DC-L14-07].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-02 marks watch or car first-class, or the product ships widgets
questions.default: design the complication or tile first, then the app; one number or status per glance
questions.preview: the metric on each glance surface.
questions.use_avoid: use tiles that are "immediate, predictable, relevant"; avoid shrinking app screens into widgets [S-L14-020; DC-L14-07].

questions.question: Does the product have AI features, and how should AI content be marked?

options.label: AI label plus an AI button variant (Carbon AI label; S2 `genai`; Atlassian Rovo) [S-L08-009, S-L08-067, S-L08-063].
AI presence as a mode on normal components
options.effect: label, explainability popover, glow tokens, revert (Carbon) [S-L14-058].

options.label: Chat components for conversational products (shadcn Message, Bubble; Carbon AI chat) [S-L08-018, S-L14-058].
Voice-only turns
options.effect: one breath, 2-5 options (Alexa) [S-L14-065].

questions.ask: Does the product generate content or act with AI? If so, how should AI content be labeled and corrected?
questions.example: Show an AI-generated summary with a label, citations, and Edit / Undo / Retry.
questions.why: Clear AI identifiers and distinct citation styling make output read as "assistive, check me"; a distinct AI accent can compete with the primary action color [DC-L13-16, DC-L08-22].
questions.default: label-button as an optional module, chat only for conversational products; label AI content, place citations next to claims, express uncertainty in high-stakes contexts, and pair every generated output with Edit, Undo and Retry
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-22, DC-L13-16, DC-L14-12; S-L13-089, S-L14-011].
questions.preview: AI output in a table cell, a side panel and a chat thread.
questions.use_avoid: use AI styling only on AI-generated content (Carbon warns against decoration); avoid human-sounding anthropomorphic framing and reasoning traces presented as explanations [DC-L14-12, DC-L13-16].

questions.question: How many token layers should sit between raw values and components?

options.label: One tier
options.effect: palette and scales used directly (Tailwind); theming means find-and-replace [DC-L07-01].

options.label: Primitive -> semantic, component tokens only when needed (Atlassian, Polaris; Fluent global + alias) [S-L07-107, S-L07-125, S-L01-033].
Primitive -> semantic -> component for every component (Material 3 comp tokens; Primer base/functional/component) [S-L07-102, S-L01-027].

questions.ask: Raw values, then semantic tokens, with component tokens only where a component must differ?
questions.example: Show `blue.600` -> `color.bg.accent` -> `button.primary.bg`, and which layer a rebrand edits.
questions.why: A semantic layer lets the look change (rebrand, new mode) without touching components; 24 of 25 benchmarked systems have one [DC-L07-01; L09 A1 row 1].
questions.default: two-plus: primitives private, semantics public, component tokens only for components a brand must restyle or values shared by 3+ components; typography as primitives, semantic composites `text.{role}.{size}` and optional component aliases
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-01, DC-L07-02, DC-L01-26, DC-L02-27]; L09 counts this as its 3-tier default with the component tier optional.
questions.preview: the token chain inspector on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use semantic tokens in every component; avoid components referencing a raw hex or px (L09: 24 of 25 systems forbid it) [L09 A1 row 1].

questions.question: Which units should the source use?

options.label: px in source, rem at the web transform (DTCG allows px and rem only; Figma imports px) [S-L07-002, S-L07-011, S-L03-037].
Unitless 4-based numbers emitted 1:1 as pt/dp/epx/px, rem for web font sizes (Fluent's ramp) [S-L10-039].
rem in source, converted down to dp/sp/CGFloat by transforms [DC-L10-08].

questions.ask: Store plain px-style numbers and convert to rem for web text?
questions.example: Show `16` becoming `1rem`, `16pt`, `16dp` and `16px`.
questions.why: px maps cleanly to pt, dp and Figma; rem respects browser zoom; unitless numbers translate 1:1 across platforms [DC-L07-11, DC-L10-08].
questions.control: single choice + toggle (spacing scales with text)
questions.default: px-to-rem (equivalently unitless numbers), rem for web type and breakpoints; "spacing scales with text size" is an explicit toggle, off by default; line height unitless
questions.preview: one value converted per platform.
questions.use_avoid: question any value not divisible by 4 (except 2, 6, 10 for icon nudges); avoid sp or rem for spacing that must not scale with text on Android [DC-L10-08; L10 baked-in rule 4].

questions.question: Which file format and build pipeline should produce platform code?

options.label: DTCG 2025.10 + Resolver, one file per tier and mode (stable since 28 Oct 2025) [S-L07-002, S-L07-004].
Terrazzo 2.x
options.effect: full DTCG including resolvers, web-strong [S-L07-179].

options.label: Style Dictionary v5
options.effect: widest native coverage (Compose, Android XML, Swift, Flutter), no resolver support, so one build per combination [S-L07-151, S-L07-162, S-L10-056].

options.label: Tokens Studio + sd-transforms, when designers author in the plugin [DC-L07-25].
Web
options.effect: CSS custom properties for semantics, media queries for preferences, container queries for components [S-L10-052, S-L10-031].

questions.ask: Export DTCG 2025.10 files with a resolver, built with Terrazzo for web or Style Dictionary for native?
questions.example: Show the output tree: CSS variables, Tailwind theme, Swift, Compose.
questions.why: The pipeline decides whether tokens arrive in each codebase in the idiom it already uses [DC-L07-25, DC-L10-22].
questions.default: dtcg-resolver as the canonical export; Terrazzo for web-only teams, Style Dictionary v5 when native outputs are needed; web-delivery on the web
questions.preview: the generated file tree with one file open.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical export and generate everything else from it; avoid hand-edited platform files [DC-L07-25].

questions.question: How should tokens be named?

options.label: Primitives
options.effect: hue + numeric step (50-950 or bounded 0-100); descriptive names only for brand colors [DC-L07-03].

options.label: Spacing primitives as percent of base (`space.200` = 16px, Atlassian, Material), semantic spacing by role [S-L03-003, S-L03-030].
A 2-4 letter prefix in platform output only (`--ds-`, `--cds-`, `--md-`); theme and brand never in names [S-L07-036, S-L07-108].
Lowercase JSON segments; kebab for CSS, camel for JS/Swift/Kotlin, snake for Android XML [S-L07-158].

questions.ask: Use `namespace.category.property.variant.state` for semantic tokens, hue plus step for colors, and a short prefix only in code output?
questions.example: Show `ds.color.bg.accent.hover`, `space.200`, and `--ds-color-bg-accent-hover` in CSS.
questions.why: Names are the shared vocabulary for humans and agents; only include the levels needed to tell tokens apart [DC-L07-04; S-L07-036].
questions.default: all five as listed
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-03, DC-L07-04, DC-L07-05, DC-L07-06, DC-L03-03].
questions.preview: a name linter that shows each token's name in JSON, CSS, Swift and Kotlin.
questions.use_avoid: use role names at the semantic tier; avoid `padding` or `margin` in primitive names and ordinal scales that look proportional but aren't [DC-L03-03].

questions.question: Which properties become tokens?

options.label: Plus radius, border width, shadow/elevation, opacity, motion [DC-L07-07].
Plus z-index, breakpoints, icon sizes, touch targets, data-viz palettes [DC-L07-07; S-L07-036].

questions.ask: Tokenize every property Figma can bind and lint, plus motion and focus?
questions.example: Show the coverage list with counts per category.
questions.why: Anything left untokenized drifts and cannot be linted or themed [DC-L07-07].
questions.default: extended; one-off illustration values stay untokenized
questions.preview: a coverage bar per category.
questions.use_avoid: use tokens for anything a lint rule should check; avoid tokenizing one-off art values [DC-L07-07].

questions.question: How should composite values (type, shadows, motion) be encoded?

options.label: Typography
options.effect: atomic primitives + semantic `typography` composites; Figma text styles with fields bound to variables (bind if more than one brand or platform) [S-L07-013, S-L07-019, S-L02-036].

options.label: Shadows and borders
options.effect: DTCG `shadow` and `border` composites; Figma effect styles with bound color and offsets [S-L07-002, S-L07-020].

options.label: Motion
options.effect: DTCG `duration`, `cubicBezier`, `transition`; Figma timing and easing variables with a reduced-motion mode; springs as `{dampingRatio, stiffness}` in `$extensions` with a bezier fallback [S-L07-033, S-L04-052].

questions.ask: Atomic primitives plus semantic composites, Figma styles bound to variables, and springs stored as extensions?
questions.example: Show a `typography` composite in JSON and the Figma text style bound to its variables.
questions.why: Composites keep a style whole for code; bound variables let styles switch with modes in Figma; DTCG has no spring type [DC-L07-12, DC-L07-13, DC-L07-14, DC-L04-28].
questions.default: all three as listed
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-12, DC-L07-13, DC-L07-14, DC-L04-28, DC-L02-28].
questions.preview: JSON and Figma views of one token of each type.
questions.use_avoid: use variables for single values that change by mode and styles for bundles; avoid hard-coded style values [DC-L07-21].

questions.question: How should themes and modes be structured so combinations don't explode?

options.label: Flatten into one axis (the DTCG resolver example
options.effect: light, lightHighContrast, dark, darkHighContrast) [S-L07-004].

options.label: Orthogonal axes, each touching a disjoint set of tokens [DC-L07-17].
Figma
options.effect: Primitives (hidden) + Semantic color + Semantic dimension (density or breakpoint) + Motion with a reduced mode [DC-L07-18].

options.label: A Breakpoint collection with 3 modes driving layout variables; grid auto layout for multi-column components [DC-L07-28; S-L07-024].

questions.ask: At most three independent axes, with high contrast as a layered override, and one Figma collection per axis?
questions.example: Show 2 schemes x 2 contrasts x 2 densities as additive collections instead of 8 flattened modes.
questions.why: Each axis multiplies QA; if two axes set the same token they should be one axis [DC-L07-17].
questions.default: orthogonal with at most 3 axes plus collections and a breakpoint collection
questions.preview: the combination count and the Figma mode budget from Q-tool-03.
questions.use_avoid: use additive collections to stay within the plan's mode limit; avoid putting brand and scheme in one flattened axis [DC-L07-18, DC-L07-27].

questions.question: How should the Figma library be kept clean?

options.label: Hide primitives from publishing; scope each semantic variable to the properties its name says [S-L07-018, S-L07-025].
Generate Web, Android and iOS code syntax from the pipeline's name transform [S-L07-018].
Variables for values, styles for bundles [S-L07-019].
Run Check designs before "Ready for dev" and review library analytics quarterly (Org/Enterprise; the builder lints on Professional) [S-L07-025, S-L07-029].

questions.ask: Hide primitives, scope every variable to its property, and generate code names automatically?
questions.example: Show a text-color variable offered only in text fill pickers.
questions.why: Hidden primitives and precise scopes keep designers on semantic tokens; generated code syntax keeps Figma and code names identical [DC-L07-19, DC-L07-20].
questions.default: all four
questions.preview: the Figma variable panel as a designer would see it.
questions.use_avoid: use scopes so a spacing token cannot be picked for a color; avoid "show in all" scopes [DC-L07-19].

questions.question: How should tokens be described and retired?

options.label: `$deprecated
options.effect: true` or "Use X instead", one release before removal [S-L07-002].

questions.ask: Give every semantic token a one-line description, and deprecate for one release before deleting?
questions.example: Show `$deprecated: "Use color.bg.accent instead"` in JSON and the warning in Figma.
questions.why: Descriptions tell people and agents what a token is for; deprecating before deleting protects consumers [DC-L07-23].
questions.default: all three
questions.preview: a token's detail card with description and status.
questions.use_avoid: use descriptions written for agents as well as people; avoid deleting tokens without a replacement [DC-L07-23].

questions.question: Which inputs should re-skin the theme, and what may other brands or clients customize?

options.label: Three generator inputs
options.effect: brand color, neutral base or temperature, contrast (Linear) [S-L06-012; DC-L06-06].

options.label: One source color plus a scheme variant and contrast level (Material) [S-L06-082, S-L06-083].
Admin UI "clicks, not code" for colors, logos, images and curated accents (Salesforce SLDS 2) [S-L06-068].

questions.ask: Let clients set brand color and logo, and allow font and radius only with previews and validation?
questions.example: Show a client admin panel with a color picker, logo upload and a live contrast check.
questions.why: Fewer inputs give more consistent, always-accessible themes but less nuance (Linear replaced 98 per-theme variables with 3 inputs); white-label customization almost always centers on color and typography [DC-L06-06, DC-L06-17; S-L06-012, S-L06-053].
questions.default: three generator inputs; clients may change brand color and logo, font and radius only with previews and validation
questions.preview: the client panel re-skinning the preview with contrast re-checked.
questions.use_avoid: use generated on-colors so client colors keep contrast; avoid exposing raw token editing to clients [DC-L06-17, DC-L06-16].

questions.question: How strict should the system be: can product teams override or extend it?

options.label: Strict
options.effect: comprehensive docs, design and code fully synced, little deviation [S-L11-018, S-L11-019].

options.label: Loose
options.effect: a framework with room to experiment [S-L11-019].

options.label: Strict canon plus product-owned "expanded universe" extensions (Dan Mall) [S-L11-014].

questions.ask: Strict core (tokens, primitives, accessibility), with product teams free to build their own patterns on top?
questions.example: Show which layers are locked and which are open under each option.
questions.why: Strict systems stay consistent but feel rigid; loose ones allow experiments but drift; a strict core with loose edges is the practical middle [DC-L11-03].
questions.default: strict core (tokens, primitives, accessibility behavior), loose edges (patterns, marketing)
questions.preview: a layer diagram with lock icons per layer.
questions.use_avoid: use a snowflake path for one-off needs; avoid forcing every product-specific component into the core [DC-L11-03, DC-L11-12].

questions.question: In what order will you build, pilot and roll out?

options.label: Foundations first
options.effect: spacing, color, type, elevation, icons, then components (Figma course order) [S-L11-009].

options.label: Pilot-driven
options.effect: extract components from a real product, apply to the next [S-L11-014].

options.label: Score pilots on common components, common patterns, high-value elements, feasibility, a champion, a 3-4 week scope, independence from legacy, marketing potential [S-L11-105].
Incremental rollout led by pain points; big-bang only with a rebrand [S-L11-105].

questions.ask: Minimal foundations first, then components proven in one pilot product, rolled out incrementally?
questions.example: Show Dan Mall's 8-criteria pilot scorecard filled for two candidate products.
questions.why: Foundations-first is tidy but abstract; pilot-driven work keeps components real; a big-bang launch creates a moment but risks pilot bias [DC-L11-06, DC-L11-07, DC-L11-08].
questions.default: minimal foundations first, then pilot-driven components, incremental rollout
questions.preview: a timeline of the plan.
questions.use_avoid: use a second pilot from a different product family to reduce bias; avoid building components no pilot needs [DC-L11-07].

questions.question: Who can contribute, and how are decisions made and recorded?

options.label: Closed or narrow
options.effect: fixes and small enhancements only (Atlassian) [S-L11-024].

options.label: Open but gated
options.effect: proposals must be useful and unique; publication must be usable, consistent, versatile (GOV.UK) [S-L11-021].

options.label: A fast lane for fixes, icons and docs; an RFC lane for new components [S-L11-020, S-L11-021].
Brad Frost's 10-step governance flow with a snowflake path [S-L11-003].
Decision records (ADRs) from day one; this questionnaire's answers map to them [S-L11-095; inferred].

questions.ask: A fast lane for fixes and icons, a proposal lane for new components, and every foundation decision logged as a decision record?
questions.example: Show a decision record generated from one of this session's answers.
questions.why: Only 36% of teams are satisfied with their contribution process; decision records explain why things are the way they are [DC-L11-11, DC-L11-12; S-L11-030].
questions.default: two-lanes, frost-flow and adrs
questions.preview: the generated decision log.
questions.use_avoid: record why an option was chosen and what it beat; avoid undocumented overrides [DC-L11-12].

questions.question: How are components labeled, versioned and retired?

options.label: Experimental > Ready > Deprecated (Primer simplified from five to three) [S-L11-025, S-L11-026].
One SemVer for the whole library while small; per-package once multi-platform [S-L11-106, S-L11-028].
Deprecate in a minor, announce with `@deprecated` and warnings, ship codemods, remove in the next major (Polaris) [S-L11-100].

questions.ask: Three statuses (experimental, ready, deprecated), one semver for the library, and deprecations removed only in the next major with a migration guide?
questions.example: Show a changelog entry with a deprecation and its codemod.
questions.why: Predictable status and versioning protect consumers; breaking changes without notice erode trust [DC-L11-13, DC-L11-14, DC-L11-15].
questions.default: status-3, semver-library, deprecation-polaris with at least one release cycle of notice; release notes every release (the most common ritual, 56%)
questions.preview: status badges in the catalog and a sample changelog.
questions.use_avoid: pair every removal with a migration path; avoid breaking changes in minor releases [DC-L11-14, DC-L11-15].

questions.question: What problem is the system solving, and how will you know it worked?

options.label: Pain
options.effect: inconsistency, speed, accessibility, rebrand, AI output drift, multi-platform parity [S-L11-083].

options.label: Design adoption (Figma analytics) and code adoption (a scanner such as Omlet or react-scanner) [S-L11-035, S-L11-037, S-L11-039].
Maturity stage
options.effect: building v1, growing adoption, surviving the teenage years, evolving (Sparkbox) [S-L11-033].

questions.ask: What hurts most today, and should we track design adoption, code adoption and a quarterly satisfaction survey?
questions.example: Show an adoption dashboard mock with the three starting metrics.
questions.why: The problem sets the success metric; most teams measure adoption, but only 5% measure ROI [DC-L11-20; S-L11-030].
questions.default: design adoption, code adoption and a quarterly survey; most builder users are at stage 1
questions.preview: the metrics dashboard mock.
questions.use_avoid: add speed or ROI studies only when leadership asks; avoid vanity counts of components [DC-L11-20].

questions.question: How will you announce the system and communicate changes?
questions.ask: Release notes every release, a public roadmap and a support channel to start?
questions.example: Show a release-note template filled from a recent change.
questions.why: Only 39% of teams are satisfied with how design-system changes are communicated [DC-L11-22; S-L11-030].
questions.default: release notes, a public roadmap and a support channel
questions.preview: the release-note template.
questions.use_avoid: use changelogs that name the migration; avoid silent releases [DC-L11-22].

questions.question: Which assistive technologies must be tested on each device class, and who owns accessibility?

options.label: VoiceOver on Apple, TalkBack on Android phone, Wear and TV, NVDA/JAWS on web [S-L14-080, S-L10-072].
Switch Control, Voice Control, Full Keyboard Access, Dwell Control [S-L14-079, S-L14-007].
Largest text
options.effect: Dynamic Type AX5, Android 200%, watch 140% [S-L10-011, S-L10-071].

questions.ask: Test one screen reader, one motor alternative and the largest text size on each device class you ship?
questions.example: Show the generated test matrix for the chosen platforms.
questions.why: Automated tools find only about 30% of issues; if a device class is first-class, its assistive technology is too [DC-L14-14; S-L11-093].
questions.control: matrix (device class x assistive tech) + text (owner)
questions.default: one screen reader, one motor alternative and the largest text size per shipped device class; a named accessibility owner (44% of teams lack a specialist)
questions.preview: the test matrix with pass/untested status per cell.
questions.use_avoid: use manual assistive-technology testing on every release candidate; avoid treating automated scans as compliance [DC-L11-19, DC-L14-14].

questions.question: How should the system leave the builder?

options.label: Copy snippets (Radix "Copy Theme", Utopia CSS) [S-L16-323, S-L16-341].
CLI install from a URL (tweakcn via shadcn) [S-L16-333, S-L16-328].
A pull request to the repository [DC-L16-12].
Push to Figma or Paper through MCP [S-L16-002, S-L16-020].
Expose the builder's generator as an MCP tool (Leonardo's example) [S-L16-338].

questions.ask: Export as CSS, a CLI install URL, DTCG files, a pull request, and a push to Figma or Paper?
questions.example: Show the export menu with one command per channel (for example `npx shadcn@latest add <url>`).
questions.why: Engineers need the output in the form they already use: a snippet, a CLI install, a token file, a pull request, or a design file [DC-L16-12].
questions.default: all six from one menu
questions.preview: the export menu and file tree.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical source for every channel (Q-tool-01); avoid channels that fork the source [DC-L16-02].

questions.question: Where do docs live, and what goes on each component page?

options.label: Figma plus Storybook (69% and 61% of teams) [S-L11-030].
A docs platform (zeroheight, Supernova) when non-engineers author [S-L11-088].
Page template
options.effect: live demo, accessibility status, when to use and not, anatomy, content rules, behaviors, per-variant guidance (Carbon Usage tab; M3 Overview/Specs/Guidelines/Accessibility) [S-L11-090, S-L08-033].

questions.ask: Generate a docs site with a page per component (usage, when not to use, live example, props, accessibility, changelog), plus a machine-readable twin?
questions.example: Show the generated Button page.
questions.why: Docs are how teams learn when and when not to use each piece; the shared core is usage guidance, live examples, API and accessibility [DC-L11-17, DC-L11-18; L09 A1 row 9].
questions.default: a generated site with the Carbon-style template plus "when not to use" and a changelog, and an llms.txt or MCP twin; docs complete is part of "done"
questions.preview: a generated component page.
questions.use_avoid: use generated "use it for / avoid it for" notes from this questionnaire on every page; avoid docs that repeat props without guidance [DC-L11-18].

questions.question: How should AI coding tools read the system?

options.label: An MCP server (Figma MCP at mcp.figma.com; Storybook MCP; shadcn MCP) [S-L11-041, S-L11-044, S-L11-045].
llms.txt and Markdown twins of docs (Cloudscape, Geist) [S-L11-048; L09 A1 row 10].

questions.ask: Ship an MCP server plus a DESIGN.md and token files, so Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Cursor build with your system?
questions.example: Show a DESIGN.md excerpt and an agent's generated button using the tokens.
questions.why: 59% of teams report UI bypassing their design system; agent channels make generated UI follow it [DC-L11-23; S-L11-031].
questions.default: at least one live channel (MCP) and one file channel (DESIGN.md + DTCG), guidelines as many short structured files
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L11-23]; L09 shared pattern row 10 (12 of 25 systems).
questions.preview: the agent-facing files and a sample agent answer.
questions.use_avoid: use evals to check agents follow the files; avoid assuming docs changes alone steer agents [DC-L11-23; S-L11-108].

questions.question: How should the system check that people and agents follow it?

options.label: Lint rules exported alongside tokens, including the behavior rules (target size, labels, one primary) [DC-L11-24; L13 E3].
Adherence scanning for raw colors and custom components (Lovable) [S-L11-053].
Drift detection at the docs layer (zeroheight MCP) [S-L11-104].

questions.ask: Export lint rules with the tokens, so every generated screen is checked against the system?
questions.example: Show a lint result: "raw hex #3b82f6, use color.bg.accent".
questions.why: Linting and structured docs cut accessibility violations per iteration from 5.1 to 0.6 when agents built with a design system (Sanity evals) [DC-L11-24; L13 E3].
questions.default: lint-rules plus evals
questions.preview: the lint report for the preview screen.
questions.use_avoid: use lint errors for Tier A rules and warnings for context-dependent ones (L13 E1); avoid automating the misapplied laws in L13 E2 (no seven-item caps) [L13 E1, E2].

questions.question: How strict should the builder's critique be?

options.label: Silent
options.effect: only automatic rules apply [DC-L15-11].

options.label: Coach
options.effect: inline messages tied to a goal, each with a one-click fix (NN/g goal-linked critique) [S-L15-075].

options.label: Strict
options.effect: block export on contrast, multiple primaries and undersized targets; warn on the rest [DC-L15-11].

options.label: Plus a metrics panel (complexity and colorfulness scores) [S-L15-047].

questions.ask: Should I coach with inline tips, stay silent, or block export on hard failures like contrast?
questions.example: Show one coach message: "Two primary buttons in this group; make one secondary."
questions.why: Messages that name the principle teach the vocabulary; strict mode blocks export on hard failures [DC-L15-11; S-L15-070].
questions.default: coach for engineers exploring; strict for teams shipping to production
questions.preview: the preview screen with messages at each level.
questions.use_avoid: accessibility failures are at least warnings in every mode; avoid silent mode for production exports [DC-L15-11].

questions.question: How should AI edits and variations work?

options.label: Agent edits arrive as reviewable patches with before/after previews [DC-L16-04].
Direct edits staged and committed together (Figma Make) [S-L16-026].
Lock + Shuffle on every parameter (shadcn create, Realtime Colors) [S-L16-327, S-L16-335].
A "show 6" grid of variants rendered on the same specimen [DC-L16-05].

questions.ask: Apply your edits instantly, show my suggestions as before/after patches, and let you lock values and shuffle the rest?
questions.example: Show a "show 6 variations" grid with two locked parameters.
questions.why: Deterministic human edits keep control; agent edits as reviewable patches keep trust; lock-and-shuffle explores without losing what you like [DC-L16-04, DC-L16-05].
questions.default: patches, lock-shuffle and show-6; vary only what is not locked
questions.preview: the variation grid.
questions.use_avoid: use variations for open, taste-driven questions (color, type, radius); avoid shuffling locked or accessibility-bound values [DC-L16-05].

questions.question: Should the builder apply optical corrections automatically?

options.label: Geometric only
options.effect: exact values [DC-L15-10].

options.label: Auto-correct known cases
options.effect: area-matched shapes (circle 112.84%), Material keylines, centroid centering, concentric nested radii [S-L15-058, S-L15-059].

questions.ask: Auto-correct known optical cases like icon sizing and nested corners, and only suggest fixes for custom assets?
questions.example: Show a circle icon at 100% vs 112.84% of a square's box.
questions.why: Geometric values can look wrong (a circle looks smaller than a square of the same box); known corrections have formulas [DC-L15-10; S-L15-058].
questions.default: auto-known for generated assets, suggest for custom assets
questions.preview: before/after pairs for each correction.
questions.use_avoid: use formulas where they exist; avoid correcting brand assets without approval [DC-L15-10].

auto_applied.rule the builder applies: Backgrounds edge-to-edge; interactive content inside platform insets plus the layout margin; nothing on a foldable hinge
Safe zones per device: nothing to read or select in the outer 5% on TV; percentage margins on round watches; car targets 24dp from edges
Nested radius: inner = max(outer - padding, smallest non-zero radius); warn on equal nested radii
Layer order as named layers spaced by 100: base < sticky < dropdown < overlay/scrim < modal < popover/tooltip < toast < skip link; no hard-coded z-index
Every translucent token ships with an opaque twin, honoring Reduce Transparency and `prefers-reduced-transparency`
Images always reserve their final box; neutral placeholder fill; skeletons only on container components
Chart chrome (titles, ticks, gridlines, legends) maps to existing text and border tokens; chart-specific tokens only for marks and interaction
Every chart gets an insight title, direct labels or shape-coded legend, a text summary and "view as table"
Docs and generated pages use a heading per section, front-loaded paragraphs, bullets for 3+ items
Each interactive component documents trigger, rules, feedback, loops and modes plus its state list
Text survives WCAG 1.4.12 overrides (line height 1.5x, paragraph 2x, letter 0.12x, word 0.16x); no fixed-height text boxes
Every text style is contrast-checked in every mode; below 18.5px bold / 24px regular it needs 4.5:1

disagreements.question: Q-plat-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Default platforms: L10 recommends web + iOS + Android phones with large-screen layouts [DC-L10-01]; survey data shows 94% of systems support web and about a third support native [S-L11-030]; L09 finds web-only most common [L09 A2 row 10].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Default to web, and show the native options with what each adds (chrome, units, targets).

disagreements.question: Q-tool-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Source of truth: L16 and L11 favor the builder's own model [DC-L16-02, DC-L11-16]; L07 favors DTCG JSON in git [DC-L07-08]; the 2026 practitioner majority says code [COMMUNITY-SIGNAL via DC-L11-16].
disagreements.what the builder should present: All four options with the drift trade-off; default builder model compiled to DTCG and code.

disagreements.question: Q-form-02
disagreements.the disagreement: Disabled submit: Carbon disables on short forms [S-L08-106]; Atlassian never disables [S-L08-085]; Material's disabled components are not focusable [S-L08-095]. BOARD also flags tooltips on disabled controls as contested.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Offer both policies; default never-disable with `aria-disabled` and helper text.

disagreements.question: Q-form-04
disagreements.the disagreement: Toasts: Primer ships none [S-L08-098]; Carbon, Atlassian and Material ship them [S-L08-079, S-L08-011, S-L08-008].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Three options; default toasts only for low-stakes results with undo.

disagreements.question: Q-form-02
disagreements.the disagreement: Validation timing: GOV.UK validates on submit [S-L08-077]; NN/g research favors on-blur for most inputs [S-L13-100].
disagreements.what the builder should present: On-blur for format checks, on submit for the rest, with the summary pattern.

disagreements.question: Q-motion-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Motion default: Material's expressive spring scheme is its default for most products [DC-L10-14; S-L10-024]; Carbon and L04 default to productive motion with bounce at or below 0.2 [DC-L04-19].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Two-mode default; springs as an explicit choice; productive cap for high-trust products.

disagreements.question: Q-state-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Focus ring: Material uses 3px [S-L04-003]; Atlassian and Primer use 2px [S-L04-016, S-L04-024]; BOARD's L13 note flags a Figma article's 3px claim as contradicting WCAG, pending the V1 verification pass.
disagreements.what the builder should present: 2px default with an offset, 3px as an option; both must meet 3:1.

disagreements.question: Q-type-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Typeface default: L02 says the system stack for productivity tools [DC-L02-01]; L09 says Inter or the system stack [DC-L09-05].
disagreements.what the builder should present: System stack by default for tools, open-neutral (Inter) as the one-click alternative.

disagreements.question: Q-type-08, Q-aud-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Body size: L02's web default is 14px UI text [DC-L02-08]; L09's regular preset is 16px [L09 A1 row 8]. They agree once density is known.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Tie body size to the density answer instead of one fixed default.

disagreements.question: Q-token-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Tiers: L07 says two tiers with component tokens only when needed [DC-L07-01]; L09 and L01 say three tiers with the component tier optional [L09 A1 row 1; DC-L01-26]. Same structure, different counting.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Present it as "primitive -> semantic, component tokens on demand".

disagreements.question: Q-color-17
disagreements.the disagreement: Contrast method: WCAG 2.2 is the enforceable standard; Radix and Geist use APCA; WCAG 3 is still a draft [DC-L01-22; BOARD L01 note].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Enforce WCAG 2.2, show APCA as advisory.

disagreements.question: Q-color-06
disagreements.the disagreement: Dynamic color: Material pushes dynamic color [DC-L01-21]; brand-led consumer apps keep fixed brand color, and iOS has no equivalent [DC-L10-05].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Per-platform choice; brand-critical and status colors always fixed.

disagreements.question: Q-space-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Base unit: 8 (Carbon, Atlassian, Material, Spectrum naming) vs 4 (Fluent, Polaris, Primer, Tailwind) [DC-L03-01].

disagreements.question: Q-shape-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Pills: Material and Spectrum 2 use pills widely [DC-L09-01]; Carbon v12 moved tags away from pills [S-L04-031]; Atlassian reserves full radius for people [S-L04-016].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Pill as an option per component role; people = full circle by default.

disagreements.question: Asset hooks
disagreements.the disagreement: Fallback order: L17's policy puts "commission a designer" before open libraries [DC-L17-04]; the icon and typeface cards default to open libraries first [DC-L05-01, DC-L02-01].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Icons and typefaces lead with open libraries (they are tool-assisted blocks); identity assets (logo, app icon, illustration, photography, sound) lead with commissioning.

disagreements.question: Quick mode
disagreements.the disagreement: L17 says owner-input blocks are never auto-decided [DC-L17-08]; Quick mode asks only 10 questions, so scope, principles and similar owner inputs take defaults.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Quick records them as "assumed" and lists them for confirmation at the end (`meta.quick_mode_assumed_owner_inputs`).

disagreements.question: Q-voice-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Capitalization: sentence case everywhere (Microsoft, Atlassian) vs title-case headings (Mailchimp) vs per element (Apple) [DC-L06-20].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Three options; sentence case by default.
